tours.title: Ballestas Islands + Paracas National Reserve
tours.shortDescription: Sail out to the Ballestas Islands and explore Paracas's most famous stretches of desert-meets-ocean scenery.
tours.description: An essential slice of the Peruvian coast in two parts. In the morning you'll sail from the El Chaco pier to the Ballestas Islands for a close-up look at the Candelabra geoglyph, sea lion colonies, and one of the country's largest concentrations of seabirds. In the afternoon you'll tour the Paracas National Reserve by vehicle, taking in the Julio C. Tello Museum, the Cathedral Viewpoint, and the postcard-perfect Red Beach and Yumaque Beach, where the desert meets the Pacific.
highlights: Boat trip to the Ballestas Islands with a view of the Candelabra geoglyph
Sea lions, seabirds, and possible dolphin or Humboldt penguin sightings
Julio C. Tello Museum and original artifacts from the Paracas culture
Red Beach and the Cathedral Viewpoint in the Paracas National Reserve
includes: Boat tour to the Ballestas Islands on an authorized vessel
Life jacket and boarding check
Local guide/assistance throughout the tour
Land transportation within the Paracas circuit
Entrance to the Paracas National Reserve
excludes: Sightseeing tickets and boarding fee, if charged separately by the operator
Transfer from Lima, unless booked as the full-day package

itinerary.title: Meet at the El Chaco Pier
itinerary.description: Check in with your assigned guide at the El Chaco Tourist Pier in Paracas Bay. Passenger registration, the boarding check required by the Port Authority, and mandatory life jackets are handled before boarding (groups of up to 44 people).
details: Reference schedule: check-in 07:15, boarding 07:45.
Bring a valid ID; the boarding check is required by the maritime authority.
A cap, sunscreen, and a light jacket are recommended for the wind offshore.

itinerary.title: Sailing to the Ballestas Islands
itinerary.description: Departure toward the Ballestas Islands, hugging the coastline to first pass the Candelabra, a massive geoglyph nearly 200 meters long carved into a hillside whose origin is still debated among researchers. The boat continues on to the archipelago, shaped by arches and caves of volcanic rock carved by the waves.
details: View of the Candelabra from the water, with no landing (it lies within the Paracas National Reserve).
The boat cruises around the islets without landing, since the area is protected for wildlife.
A great time for photos, thanks to morning light and calmer seas.

itinerary.title: Touring the archipelago: marine wildlife and seabirds
itinerary.description: A slow cruise around the islands for a close look at sea lions and, occasionally, Humboldt penguins, plus one of Peru's largest concentrations of seabirds: guanay cormorants, Peruvian boobies, pelicans, and Inca terns. The guide explains the history of guano extraction on the island, once key to Peru's 19th-century economy.
details: Wildlife viewing with no landing; the boat gets close enough for zoom-lens photos.
Dolphins are sometimes spotted along the way, though not guaranteed.
A camera with a good zoom lens or binoculars are recommended.

itinerary.title: Return to the El Chaco Pier
itinerary.description: Sail back to Paracas. After disembarking, there's a short break at El Chaco to use the restrooms, grab a drink, or browse the craft stalls before continuing on to the Paracas National Reserve.
details: Reference disembarking time: 10:00 to 10:15.
Free time: 15 to 20 minutes.
Meeting point for the land segment: the pier's esplanade.

itinerary.title: Paracas National Reserve: Julio C. Tello Museum and viewpoints
itinerary.description: Entry into the Paracas National Reserve by tourist vehicle. The first stop is the Julio C. Tello Museum, which displays original Paracas-culture artifacts (pottery, textiles, and tools), followed by photo stops at the Cathedral Viewpoint — a seaside rock formation damaged but not destroyed by the 2007 earthquake — and the Supay Beach Viewpoint.
details: Reference schedule: reserve entry 11:00, Julio C. Tello Museum 11:15.
Reserve entry ticket included in the tour (reference fee S/ 11).
Short photo stops at the viewpoints, with no long walking involved.

itinerary.title: Red Beach and Yumaque Beach
itinerary.description: Visit Red Beach, one of Peru's most photographed spots for the contrast between the yellow desert, the reddish (volcanic-origin) sand, and the turquoise sea. Continue on to Yumaque Beach, a more sheltered bay where seabirds — and, in season, flamingos nearby — can occasionally be spotted.
details: Reference schedule: Red Beach 12:30, Yumaque Beach 13:15.
Free time at Red Beach for photos and a walk along the shore, about 20 minutes.
Swimming isn't recommended; currents in the area can be strong.

itinerary.title: End of service
itinerary.description: Return to the original meeting point in Paracas, where the service ends. If your itinerary continues on to Ica or Huacachina, coordinate the transport connection with your guide according to the tour package you booked.
details: Reference finish time: 14:00 to 14:30.
Optional connection to Ica/Huacachina available on request.
Bring water; there aren't many vendors inside the reserve.

tours.title: Paracas, Ballestas Islands and Huacachina from Lima
tours.shortDescription: A 17-hour full-day trip from Lima combining the boat trip to the Ballestas Islands, a pisco winery in Ica, and dune buggy and sandboarding adventure at the Huacachina oasis.
tours.description: A long, action-packed day that departs Lima before dawn to make the most of a full day in Peru's near south. After three and a half hours on the Panamericana Sur highway you'll reach Paracas to sail out to the Ballestas Islands for a close-up look at the Candelabra, sea lions, and seabirds. From there, continue on to Ica to visit a traditional pisco winery, then wrap up the afternoon at Huacachina, the oasis ringed by giant sand dunes, with a dune buggy ride and sandboarding before the drive back to Lima that night.
highlights: Boat trip to the Ballestas Islands with a view of the Candelabra geoglyph
Sea lions and seabirds around the archipelago
Pisco and wine tasting at an Ica winery
Dune buggy ride across the sands of Huacachina
Sandboarding as the sun sets over the oasis
A full day out from Lima, all in a single trip
includes: Round-trip tourist transportation from pickup points in Lima
Boat tour to the Ballestas Islands with life jacket
Entry and tasting at an Ica pisco winery
Dune buggy circuit and sandboard at Huacachina
Guide/driver assistance throughout the tour
excludes: Hotel pickup outside the listed meeting areas

itinerary.title: Departure from Lima
itinerary.description: Pickup at meeting points in Miraflores, San Isidro, and nearby areas (or at your hotel, depending on the package booked) to start the drive south along the Panamericana Sur. The trip to Paracas takes about three and a half hours.
details: Reference meeting point: Panamericana Sur junction or hotel lobby, depending on booking.
Eat breakfast before pickup; no breakfast stop is included.
Bring a valid ID for checkpoints along the way.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Paracas and boarding at El Chaco
itinerary.description: Arrival at the El Chaco Tourist Pier in Paracas Bay. Passenger registration, the Port Authority's boarding check, and life jackets are handled before boarding the boat to the Ballestas Islands.
details: Reference boarding time: 08:00 to 08:15.
Groups of up to 44 passengers per authorized vessel.
A cap, sunscreen, and light jacket are recommended for the offshore wind.

itinerary.title: Sailing to the Ballestas Islands
itinerary.description: Departure toward the archipelago, hugging the coast to first pass the Candelabra, the geoglyph carved into a hillside. The boat continues among arches and caves of volcanic rock to spot sea lions, Humboldt penguins, and one of the country's largest concentrations of seabirds.
details: Sailing with no landing; the islands are a protected area within the Paracas National Reserve.
Total sailing time: about 1 h 45 min round trip.
A great time for photos: morning light and calmer seas.

itinerary.title: Transfer from Paracas to Ica
itinerary.description: Disembark at El Chaco and set off by road toward the city of Ica, the heart of Peru's pisco and wine production. The trip takes around an hour and a quarter.
details: Brief free time at the pier before continuing (10 to 15 min).
Approximate distance from Paracas to Ica: 75 km.
A good time to hydrate; Ica's climate is drier and hotter.

itinerary.title: Pisco winery in Ica
itinerary.description: Visit to a traditional winery (such as El Catador) to learn about the artisanal process of distilling pisco and making wine. Includes a tasting of pure and acholado piscos and local wines, with free time to have lunch on your own at the winery's restaurants.
details: Guided walk through the stills and fermentation vats (~30 min).
Tasting of 5 to 7 varieties of pisco and wine.
Lunch not included; Creole food options are available on site.

itinerary.title: Huacachina: oasis, buggy, and sandboarding
itinerary.description: Arrival at the Huacachina oasis, surrounded by dunes up to 100 meters high. Free time to stroll beside the lagoon, followed by an approximately 2-hour dune buggy circuit through the sand, with stops to try sandboarding on slopes of varying difficulty.
details: Safety briefing and mandatory seatbelt before boarding the buggy.
Sandboard included; no prior experience required.
The afternoon schedule lets you finish with sunset over the dunes.

itinerary.title: Return to Lima
itinerary.description: Departure from Huacachina/Ica back to Lima. The return trip takes between 4 and 4.5 hours depending on traffic along the Panamericana Sur, arriving back at the original pickup points.
details: Estimated arrival in Lima: between 21:30 and 22:00.
Have dinner before pickup or bring snacks for the road.
Times may vary due to traffic or weather conditions on the route.

tours.title: Buggy and Sandboarding in Huacachina
tours.shortDescription: A 2-hour dune buggy circuit through the sands of Huacachina with stops for sandboarding, ideal for the sunset run.
tours.description: A short, high-impact activity for travelers with limited time in Ica. A dune buggy with an authorized driver climbs and descends the giant dunes surrounding the Huacachina oasis, stopping at the highest ridges to try sandboarding and take in panoramic photos. The 4:00 pm departure is the most popular, since the circuit wraps up with the sunset painting the dunes in shades of orange.
highlights: Dune buggy ride across dunes up to 100 meters high
Sandboarding on slopes for beginners and advanced riders
Panoramic views of the Huacachina oasis
Sunset over the dunes on the 4:00 pm departure
A short activity, easy to combine with other Ica tours
includes: Authorized buggy driver
Sandboard and wax
Seatbelt in the buggy
Shared dune circuit (small group)
excludes: Municipal entry fee to the oasis area, if charged separately by the operator
Professional photos or video during the tour

itinerary.title: Meet at Huacachina
itinerary.description: Check in at the departure point beside the Huacachina lagoon and get your buggy assignment. The driver gives a short safety briefing: mandatory seatbelt use, how to hold on properly on the descents, and signals to use during sandboarding.
details: Meeting point: the boardwalk around the Huacachina lagoon.
Groups of up to 8 people per buggy.
Comfortable clothing, sunglasses, and something to cover your nose and mouth from the sand are recommended.

itinerary.title: Departure by buggy toward the dunes
itinerary.description: The buggy leaves the oasis and starts climbing the first dunes of the Ica desert. The driver looks for the ridges with the best views for the tour's first photo stops.
details: The first few minutes are on gentle climbs to get used to the buggy's movement.
A short stop for panoramic photos of the oasis from above.
The route is shared with other buggies from the same operator.

itinerary.title: First sandboarding stop
itinerary.description: The first dune set up for sandboarding, with a gentle slope, ideal for learning the lying-down position on the board and trying the descent with no prior experience.
details: A board and wax are provided at each stop.
The descent is done lying face-down; no snowboarding technique is required.
The driver loads the boards back onto the buggy after each run.

itinerary.title: Steeper dunes
itinerary.description: The buggy heads to the section with the tour's tallest dunes, where the sandboarding runs are steeper for those wanting more speed. Between stops there are stretches of fast driving along the sand ridges.
details: Suitable for those who already tried the previous stop.
Anyone who'd rather not ride down can stay in the buggy and simply enjoy the drive.
A great stretch for action shots with a camera or phone secured with a strap.

itinerary.title: Sunset viewpoint
itinerary.description: Final stop at one of the circuit's highest dunes to watch the sunset over the desert and the Huacachina oasis in the distance, the most photographed moment of the tour.
details: The best light of the tour, with the sun low over the dunes.
10 to 15 minutes of free time for photos.
Bring a light jacket; the temperature drops quickly once the sun sets.

itinerary.title: Return to Huacachina
itinerary.description: Final descent through the dunes back to the oasis, arriving at the same meeting point where the service ends.
details: Estimated arrival: 18:00 to 18:15.
Service ends at the Huacachina boardwalk.
The circuit is also offered on the 9:00 am, 11:00 am, and 2:00 pm departures, with a similar 2-hour duration.

tours.title: Flight Over the Nazca Lines
tours.shortDescription: A 30- to 35-minute scenic flight over the main Nazca Lines figures, departing from the María Reiche Airfield.
tours.description: A small-plane overflight operated by companies certified by Peru's Civil Aeronautics Authority (DGAC), taking off from the María Reiche Airfield, just minutes from the city of Nazca. The flight zigzags over the desert's most famous figures: the hummingbird, the monkey, the spider, the condor, and the tree and hands, among others. The morning slot is recommended, when wind and turbulence over the desert tend to be lower.
highlights: Flight over the hummingbird, monkey, spider, and condor figures
Departure from the María Reiche Airfield, near Nazca
Morning slot with less turbulence
Aircraft with passenger weigh-in and pre-flight checks
Flight certificate at the end, depending on the operator
includes: Hotel-airfield-hotel transfer in Nazca
Check-in and passenger weigh-in procedures
Pre-flight safety briefing
30- to 35-minute scenic overflight
Flight certificate, depending on the operator
excludes: Airport fee, paid at the airfield (reference S/ 25)
Transfer from Ica or Lima to Nazca
Extra charge for excess weight (over 95 kg per passenger, depending on the airline)

itinerary.title: Pickup at your Nazca hotel
itinerary.description: Transfer from your hotel in Nazca to the María Reiche Airfield, about 4 km from downtown, roughly a 10-minute drive.
details: Travelers arriving from Ica or Lima should arrange the transfer to Nazca in advance.
Bring your original ID document; it's required for the flight manifest.
There's no special dress code for the flight.

itinerary.title: Check-in and passenger weigh-in
itinerary.description: Check-in at the airline counter: booking and ID verification, plus mandatory individual weigh-in to calculate weight distribution inside the small plane.
details: Passengers over 95 kg may require an extra seat or additional charge, depending on the airline.
Aircraft operate with a capacity of 6 to 12 passengers, depending on the model.
Pay the airport fee at this point if it isn't already included.

itinerary.title: Safety briefing and boarding
itinerary.description: Safety briefing led by the pilot or ground staff: seatbelt use, what to do in case of motion sickness, and tips for spotting the figures from the windows during the turns.
details: Flights with a pilot and co-pilot at most certified operators.
Avoid a heavy meal beforehand if you're prone to motion sickness.
Motion sickness bags available on board as a precaution.

itinerary.title: Overflight of the Nazca Lines
itinerary.description: Takeoff and a zigzag route over the desert to fly over 8 to 13 figures, depending on the operator's route: the hummingbird, the monkey, the spider, the condor, the tree and hands, among others. The pilot tilts the plane to each side so both rows of seats can see and photograph the figures.
details: Flight duration: 30 to 35 minutes depending on the number of figures included in the route.
Sharp turns are normal; they're part of the maneuver to show each figure to both sides.
Best visibility in the morning, before the wind kicks up more dust from the desert.

itinerary.title: Landing and flight certificate
itinerary.description: Landing at the María Reiche Airfield. Some operators hand out a commemorative certificate or diploma for the flight before you leave the boarding area.
details: Wait time for the certificate: 5 to 10 minutes.
Crafts and souvenirs available for purchase at the airfield.
Restrooms available at the terminal.

itinerary.title: Return to the hotel
itinerary.description: Transfer back to your hotel in Nazca, where the service ends. The total schedule may run longer due to air traffic delays or wind conditions, which are common at this airfield.
details: Estimated finish time: between 09:45 and 10:30 depending on the slot.
The overflight is also offered on the 9:00, 10:00, and 11:00 am slots.
Flights may be rescheduled at the pilot's discretion due to bad weather; the exact time isn't guaranteed.

tours.title: Colca Canyon Full Day from Arequipa
tours.shortDescription: A roughly 14-hour full-day trip from Arequipa to Colca Canyon, with the condor's flight at the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint, Andean villages, and the option of hot springs.
tours.description: One of the longest and most complete trips departing from Arequipa. It leaves before dawn to reach Chivay in time for breakfast and acclimatization before heading up to the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint, where between 8:00 and 9:30 am you're most likely to see Andean condors soaring over the canyon. The rest of the day takes in the villages of Maca and Yanque, with the option to relax in the La Calera hot springs before a buffet lunch and the long drive back to Arequipa past the Patapampa volcano viewpoint.
highlights: Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint with the flight of the Andean condor
Traditional villages of Maca and Yanque
Pre-Hispanic terraces of the Colca Valley
La Calera hot springs (optional)
Patapampa viewpoint at 4,910 m above sea level on the return
Salinas y Aguada Blanca National Reserve, home to vicuñas
includes: Round-trip tourist transportation from Arequipa
Professional guide throughout the tour
Pickup from hotels in the central area
Breakfast and buffet lunch stops in Chivay (meals not included)
Assistance throughout the tour
excludes: Colca tourist ticket (reference S/ 70, paid at Patapampa or Chivay)
Entry to the La Calera hot springs (reference S/ 15)

itinerary.title: Departure from Arequipa
itinerary.description: Pickup from hotels in the central area and departure by tourist bus toward the Colca Valley. The route climbs to the volcano viewpoint before descending into Chivay.
details: Pickup time: between 02:50 and 03:20 depending on the hotel.
Bring warm clothing; temperatures drop several degrees below zero along the way.
The first leg of the trip takes about 3 hours; it's normal to sleep on the bus.

itinerary.title: Chivay: breakfast and acclimatization
itinerary.description: Stop in Chivay (3,635 m above sea level) for breakfast on your own and to acclimatize before continuing toward the canyon. It's the valley's largest town and the starting point for Cruz del Cóndor.
details: Breakfast not included; several restaurants near Chivay's main square.
Stop length: approximately 45 minutes.
A good place to buy coca leaf tea for the altitude.

itinerary.title: Route to Cruz del Cóndor
itinerary.description: The bus continues along the canyon's edge past the villages of Yanque and Achoma, with progressive views of the Colca Valley and its terraces, in use since pre-Inca times.
details: Chivay to Cruz del Cóndor: about 1 hour.
Short photo stops at intermediate viewpoints depending on the group.
The canyon reaches over 3,400 meters deep at its lowest point.

itinerary.title: Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint
itinerary.description: The day's main stop at the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint, at 3,600 m above sea level, where morning thermal currents send Andean condors soaring close to visitors. Sightings aren't 100% guaranteed, but the window between 8:00 and 9:30 am tends to see the most activity.
details: Free time at the viewpoint: 45 minutes to 1 hour.
The Colca tourist ticket is paid or checked at this point.
Avoid bright colors and getting too close to the viewpoint's edge.

itinerary.title: Villages of Maca and Yanque
itinerary.description: A tour through the village of Maca, with its colonial church and active terraces, and Yanque, known for its main square. Both preserve architecture and customs from the Collagua and Cabana cultures.
details: Photo stop at the terraces of Maca (~20 min).
Visit to the Church of the Immaculate Conception in Yanque, schedule permitting.
Local textile handicraft stalls in both villages.

itinerary.title: La Calera hot springs (optional)
itinerary.description: Stop in Chivay for anyone wanting to relax at the La Calera hot springs, with mineral-water pools between 35 and 38 degrees, 3 km from town. An optional activity for those who'd rather rest before lunch.
details: Entry not included, reference S/ 15.
Five pools of different sizes and temperatures.
Bring swimwear and a towel if you'd like to go in.

itinerary.title: Buffet lunch in Chivay
itinerary.description: Buffet-style lunch at one of Chivay's tourist restaurants, with regional dishes such as guinea pig, alpaca, and trout, before setting off on the long drive back to Arequipa.
details: Lunch not included in the base price; paid at the restaurant.
Lunch time: approximately 1 hour.
Last chance to buy local textile handicrafts.

itinerary.title: Return to Arequipa via Patapampa
itinerary.description: Departure from Chivay to Arequipa along the high route, with a stop at the Patapampa volcano viewpoint (4,910 m above sea level) and passing through the Salinas y Aguada Blanca National Reserve, home to wild vicuñas.
details: Photo stop at Patapampa, the highest point on the route.
Possible sightings of vicuñas and other camelids in the reserve.
Estimated arrival in Arequipa: between 17:00 and 18:00.

tours.title: Colca Canyon 2D/1N
tours.shortDescription: Two unhurried days to cross the Salinas y Aguada Blanca Reserve, sleep in Chivay, and watch the Andean condor fly at the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint.
tours.description: A classic Colca itinerary designed for travelers who'd rather not do the full circuit in a single day. The route crosses the Salinas y Aguada Blanca National Reserve, spotting vicuñas and stopping at the Patapampa volcano viewpoint, then descends into the Colca Valley to spend the night in Chivay, with the option of a soak in the La Calera hot springs, and on the second day arrives early at the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint to watch the Andean condor take flight before returning to Arequipa or connecting on to Puno.
highlights: Crossing the Salinas y Aguada Blanca National Reserve with vicuña sightings
Patapampa volcano viewpoint at 4,910 m above sea level
An overnight rest stop in the town of Chivay
Optional soak in the La Calera hot springs
The Andean condor's flight at the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint
Antahuilque and Choquetico viewpoints with pre-Inca terraces
includes: Tourist transportation Arequipa – Chivay – Colca (return to Arequipa or connection to Puno, depending on the package booked)
Professional Spanish-speaking guide
Pickup from a hotel in central Arequipa
1 night's accommodation in Chivay (category according to the package booked)
Lunch on day 1
excludes: Colca tourist ticket (entry to Cruz del Cóndor and the valley's terraces)
Entry to the La Calera hot springs
Dinner on day 1 and lunch on day 2
Connection to Puno if not booked together with the package

itinerary.title: Arequipa - Salinas y Aguada Blanca Reserve - Chivay
itinerary.description: Pickup at your hotel and departure via the Yura route, skirting the Chachani volcano, toward the Salinas y Aguada Blanca National Reserve, where vicuñas are commonly spotted on the Cañahuas plain. Photo stop at the Patapampa volcano viewpoint, at 4,910 m above sea level, with views of the Ampato, Sabancaya, Hualca Hualca, and Ubinas volcanoes. Descent into the Colca Valley and arrival in Chivay for lunch; in the afternoon, free time for the La Calera hot springs and, optionally, dinner with a folk show.
details: Reference schedule: pickup 07:30-08:00, Patapampa viewpoint 10:30, arrival in Chivay 12:30.
Highest point of the day at Patapampa: 4,910 m above sea level; hydration and warm clothing are recommended.
Free afternoon from about 15:00 for the La Calera hot springs (entry not included).

itinerary.title: Cruz del Cóndor and return, or connection to Puno
itinerary.description: Very early departure from Chivay to the Cruz del Cóndor viewpoint, the highest point of the canyon for watching the Andean condor take flight, which usually happens between 8:00 and 10:00 am on the thermal currents. The return includes stops at the Antahuilque and Choquetico viewpoints, with views of pre-Inca terraces and ancestral tombs, plus the villages of Maca and Yanque. From Chivay or Cabanaconde, passengers connecting to Puno can catch the regional bus to the altiplano.
details: Reference schedule: breakfast 05:30, departure to Cruz del Cóndor 06:00, condor flight viewing 08:00-10:00.
Return with photo stops at Antahuilque, Choquetico, Maca, and Yanque before descending to Arequipa.
Reference arrival in Arequipa 14:00-15:00; connection to Puno (additional service, not included) departs Chivay between 10:00 and 13:00.
itinerary.distance: Cruz del Cóndor-Arequipa ~160 km (~4 h) or Chivay-Puno connection ~4-5 h

tours.title: Uros and Taquile Full Day on Lake Titicaca
tours.shortDescription: A full day sailing across Lake Titicaca, from the floating Uros Islands to Taquile Island, an Intangible Cultural Heritage site for its textile art.
tours.description: A classic Puno tour combining two very different Titicaca communities. It starts with a visit to the artificial Uros Islands, built and maintained from totora reeds, then sails nearly two hours to Taquile Island, where a walk along stone paths leads up to the main square and a viewpoint with 360-degree views of the lake. The day includes a traditional lunch on Taquile and wraps up with the return sail to Puno in the late afternoon.
highlights: Floating Uros Islands built from totora reeds
Scenic sailing across Lake Titicaca, the world's highest navigable lake
Taquile Island and its UNESCO-recognized textile art
Taquile viewpoint at 3,950 m above sea level with 360-degree views
Traditional lunch made with local ingredients
Direct contact with Uros and Taquileño families
includes: Transfer from your hotel in Puno to the port
Tourist boat with life jackets
Professional Spanish-speaking guide
Entry to the Uros and Taquile islands
Traditional lunch on Taquile
excludes: Optional ride on a traditional totora reed raft at the Uros islands

itinerary.title: Pickup and boarding at Puno port
itinerary.description: Transfer from your hotel to Puno's main port and check-in to board the tourist boat. Life jackets are handed out before departing toward the Uros Islands.
details: Reference departure time: 07:00 to 07:30.
Bring warm clothing; the morning sail on Titicaca is cold, above 3,800 m elevation.
Sunscreen recommended; UV exposure is high at this altitude.

itinerary.title: Floating Uros Islands
itinerary.description: About a 30-minute sail through the totora reed beds to one of the more than 100 artificial Uros islands, each home to between 3 and 10 families. Residents explain how they cut, dry, and weave the totora reed to keep the island afloat and to build rafts that last up to 7 years.
details: Demonstration of island construction and, depending on the island, of a totora reed raft.
Option to ride a traditional raft for an extra fee (not included).
Visit length: approximately 45 minutes to 1 hour.

itinerary.title: Sailing to Taquile
itinerary.description: Departure from Uros toward Taquile Island, about 35 km from Puno's port. The crossing over Titicaca's open waters takes about 2 hours, with views of the lake and, on clear days, the Bolivian cordillera in the distance.
details: Sailing time: 1 h 30 min to 2 hours depending on the boat.
A good stretch to rest or chat with the guide about the lake's culture.
Restrooms available on board on most boats.

itinerary.title: Arrival at Taquile and walk to the main square
itinerary.description: Disembark at one of Taquile's docks and walk up 533 stone steps built by the community itself, with intermediate viewpoints over the lake along the way, up to the main square at 3,950 m above sea level.
details: Walking time: 25 to 35 minutes at an easy pace.
The path climbs in stretches, not a continuous staircase.
A slow pace is recommended due to the altitude; bring water.

itinerary.title: Cultural tour and viewpoint
itinerary.description: Visit to Taquile's main viewpoint, with 360-degree views of Titicaca, and an explanation of Taquileño textile art, declared an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO in 2005. The men knit while walking with two needles, and the type of chullo hat or the color of the woven belt communicates the wearer's marital status or social role.
details: Residents weave in the square and sell textiles directly.
The guide explains the symbolism of the chullo hats and belts.
Free time for photos and shopping: approximately 30 minutes.

itinerary.title: Traditional lunch on Taquile
itinerary.description: Lunch at a community restaurant on Taquile featuring local ingredients: lake trout, quinoa, and fava beans, among others. The meal is prepared by island families as part of the community-based tourism model.
details: Set menu with a vegetarian option available on request.
The lunch is part of the community tourism that sustains the island.
Lunch time: approximately 1 hour.

itinerary.title: Return to Puno
itinerary.description: Descend to Taquile's dock via a different, shorter route than the ascent, then sail directly back to Puno, with no stop at Uros.
details: Walk down to the dock: 15 to 20 minutes via an alternate staircase.
Return sailing time: approximately 2 to 2.5 hours.
Estimated arrival in Puno: between 16:00 and 16:30.

tours.title: Titicaca Homestay: Uros, Amantaní and Taquile 2D/1N
tours.shortDescription: Two days to experience Lake Titicaca up close: the floating Uros Islands, a homestay night with a family on Amantaní, and Taquile's textile culture.
tours.description: An unhurried journey across the world's highest navigable lake, at a different pace from the classic full-day tour. It combines a visit to the floating totora-reed Uros Islands, a night staying with a local family on Amantaní Island — with dinner, a sunset walk, and the option of a traditional dance — and a stop in Taquile, recognized by UNESCO for its textile art, before sailing back to Puno.

itinerary.title: Puno - Uros Islands - Amantaní
itinerary.description: Pickup at your hotel and transfer to Puno's port to board the tourist boat. After a 30-40 minute sail you'll reach the floating Uros Islands, built entirely from totora reeds, where the guide explains their way of life, with the option of a short ride on a traditional raft. Continue for nearly 3 hours to Amantaní, where local families welcome visitors into their homes; in the afternoon there's free time to walk up to the Pachatata or Pachamama hills and watch the sunset over the lake, followed by dinner with the family and, optionally, a traditional dance with local music.

Overnight with a host family in simple rooms; warm clothing and a flashlight are recommended.

itinerary.title: Amantaní - Taquile - Puno

tours.title: Laguna 69 Full-Day Trek from Huaraz
tours.shortDescription: A one-day trek to Laguna 69, one of the most famous turquoise lakes in the Cordillera Blanca.

tours.title: Llanganuco Lakes and Yungay Campo Santo Memorial
tours.shortDescription: A full-day tour from Huaraz through the Callejón de Huaylas to the Llanganuco lakes, taking in the Campo Santo memorial in Yungay and close-up views of Huascarán.
tours.description: One of the most popular one-day circuits in the Áncash highlands, combining nature, history, and high-mountain scenery without any trekking required. The route heads north from Huaraz through the Callejón de Huaylas, passing through Carhuaz and its handmade ice cream, before reaching Yungay, where the Campo Santo memorial commemorates the 1970 landslide that buried the town. The heart of the day is the entrance to Huascarán National Park through the Llanganuco ravine, where turquoise Lake Chinancocha lies at the foot of the Huascarán and Huandoy peaks. The return trip includes stops in Caraz and the craft village of Taricá before arriving back in Huaraz at dusk.

Campo Santo de Yungay, memorial to the 1970 landslide
Handmade ice cream and the main square in Carhuaz

One-day circuit with no trekking or prior acclimatization required

itinerary.title: Yungay and the Campo Santo memorial
itinerary.description: Arrival in the district of Yungay, where the guide explains the earthquake of May 31, 1970, and the landslide that buried the old town, claiming thousands of lives. The Campo Santo, today a memorial with gardens and the palm trees that once marked the old main square, is one of the most historically significant sites in the region.

Altitude of Lake Chinancocha: approximately 3,850 m (12,630 ft) above sea level.

itinerary.title: Lake Chinancocha: free time and lunch

Stop in Taricá: 15 to 20 minutes depending on traffic and timing.

tours.title: Pastoruri: Climate Change Route
tours.shortDescription: A high-mountain full-day tour from Huaraz to the Pastoruri glacier, featuring lakes, natural sparkling springs, Puya Raimondi forests, and an educational walk about glacial retreat.
tours.description: A high-altitude excursion into the southern sector of Huascarán National Park, designed as a hands-on lesson in climate change. The route climbs from Huaraz through Recuay, Ticapampa, and Cátac to the Pachacoto ravine, with stops at Lake Patococha, the natural sparkling springs of Pumapampa, and a forest of Puya Raimondi, the largest endemic plant in the Andes. The highlight is a short walk to the base of the Pastoruri glacier, above 5,000 m (16,400 ft), where the guide points out the visible retreat of the ice over recent decades. Given the demands of the altitude, it's recommended to spend at least one day acclimatizing in Huaraz (3,052 m / 10,013 ft) before taking this tour.

Puya Raimondi forest, the largest bromeliad in the world
Lake Patococha and the natural sparkling springs of Pumapampa

itinerary.title: Pachacoto ravine and Lake Patococha

Photo stop of 10 to 15 minutes.
Possible sightings of wild ducks and other high-Andean birds.

itinerary.title: Puya Raimondi forest
itinerary.description: Visit to one of the most accessible Puya Raimondi forests in the Cordillera Blanca. This plant, endemic to the Andes, can live for more than eighty years, flowers just once with a spike up to 12 meters (39 ft) tall, and then dies — a life cycle the guide explains during the stop.
details: Stop of 15 to 20 minutes for photos and a short walk among the plants.

Protected species; do not touch or cut the plants.

itinerary.title: Pumapampa sparkling springs

itinerary.title: Pastoruri base and walk to the glacier
itinerary.description: Arrival at the Pastoruri base parking area, the starting point of the Climate Change Route, a signposted trail of about 3.5 km (2.2 mi) round trip that climbs gently to a viewpoint close to the glacier's face, above 5,000 m (16,400 ft). tours.title: Laguna Azul Full Day from Tarapoto
tours.shortDescription: A San Martín classic: crossing the Huallaga River by ferry raft, a boat ride, and an afternoon at the lakeside beach of Laguna Azul in Sauce.
tours.description: A classic full-day excursion through San Martín's high jungle to Laguna Azul, a turquoise mirror of water ringed by hills in the district of Sauce. The route heads south along the Marginal Highway to Puerto López, crosses the Huallaga River on a cable-guided ferry raft, and continues on to the lakeshore, where a motorboat ride takes you across the water before arriving at the El Caño recreation area. There you'll have free time to swim, relax in a hammock, and try optional activities like kayaking, horseback riding, or jet skiing, plus a lunch of regional specialties. It's an easy-going outing, perfect for families and travelers looking for nature and relaxation without a demanding trek.

tours.title: Ahuashiyacu Waterfall + Lamas from Tarapoto
tours.shortDescription: Waterfall, natural pool, and Kechwa-Lamista culture on an easy one-day route from Tarapoto.
tours.description: A full day built around two of San Martín's signature attractions. In the morning, visit Ahuashiyacu Waterfall, a 40-plus-meter cascade surrounded by rainforest just 30 minutes from Tarapoto, with free time to swim in its natural pool. tours.shortDescription: Cover Tarapoto's three must-sees in 3 days: the Kechwa-Lamista town of Lamas, Laguna Azul in Sauce, and Ahuashiyacu Waterfall, with daily departures from the city.

Day one is dedicated to Lamas, San Martín's 'folkloric capital' and home to the Kechwa-Lamista people; day two to Laguna Azul in Sauce, with a boat ride and an afternoon at the lakeside beach; and day three to Ahuashiyacu Waterfall, an easily accessible cascade surrounded by tropical rainforest. Tarapoto serves as a fixed base throughout the trip, with daily returns to the city. It's an ideal option for couples, families, or travelers short on time who want nature, living culture, and relaxation all in one program.

The visit also includes the lookout and Lamas Castle before returning to Tarapoto.

tours.title: Tambopata and Lake Sandoval 3D/2N
tours.shortDescription: Escape to Peru's southern Amazon and discover Lake Sandoval, the most iconic oxbow lake in the Tambopata National Reserve, on a short program that's the perfect first taste of the rainforest.
tours.description: A three-day program designed for travelers short on time who still want to experience the Amazon rainforest in an authentic way. From Puerto Maldonado you'll navigate the Madre de Dios River to a lodge deep inside the Tambopata National Reserve, your starting point for the walk to Lake Sandoval, a 127-hectare oxbow lake ringed by aguaje palm swamps and home to families of giant river otters, black caimans, and dozens of bird species. The itinerary blends short walks, a glide across the lake in a silent paddle boat, and a nighttime wildlife outing, making this the most accessible Amazon program in our catalog.

From there, a roughly 40-minute boat ride takes you to the lodge, set deep inside the Tambopata National Reserve. After check-in and a welcome drink made from local fruits, enjoy an interpretive walk along nearby trails, and as night falls, a boat excursion to spot caimans by flashlight.

After a 3 km walk through varillal and aguaje-palm forest, you'll board a paddle boat (motor-free, so as not to disturb the wildlife) and glide across much of the lake's 127 hectares in search of giant river otter families, black caimans, monkeys, and birds such as the hoatzin. In the afternoon, there's time to climb an observation tower and visit a Brazil nut harvesters' camp before dinner.

Roughly 40-minute return boat ride down the Madre de Dios River.
20-minute stop at the local market before the transfer to the airport/terminal.

tours.title: Tambopata + Chuncho Clay Lick 4D/3N
tours.shortDescription: Head deep up the Tambopata River to the Chuncho clay lick (Collpa Chuncho), one of the largest macaw clay licks in the Amazon, on a four-day program built for birdwatchers and lovers of deep rainforest.
tours.description: A four-day program that moves off the beaten path, traveling upriver on the Tambopata River to the area around the Chuncho clay lick, a mineral clay wall where, every morning at dawn, dozens of macaws and parrots gather in a spectacle of color and sound. The itinerary includes two full days of interpretive walks through terra firme forest, nighttime wildlife outings, activities such as canoeing or piranha fishing, before culminating in an early-morning visit to the clay lick. Since it requires more travel time than a lake-based program, this is the recommended option for travelers seeking a deeper immersion into the Tambopata National Reserve.

In the afternoon, a short orientation walk, and after dinner, the first nighttime outing with flashlights in search of spiders, frogs, and other nocturnal wildlife.

In the afternoon, canoeing or piranha fishing on a nearby oxbow lake or stream, depending on the season and river level. Viewing takes place in silence from a covered shelter, with breakfast served during the wait. In the afternoon, return to the lodge for lunch and free time before a farewell dinner.

tours.title: Iquitos Amazon Lodge 3D/2N

tours.title: Kuélap Full Day from Chachapoyas
tours.shortDescription: A pre-Inca stone fortress, a cable car over the Tingo canyon, and Chachapoya culture in a full day from Chachapoyas.
tours.description: A full day to one of Peru's most important archaeological complexes: the fortress of Kuélap, built in stone by the Chachapoya culture atop a ridge at 3,000 meters above sea level. The route departs Chachapoyas for Nuevo Tingo, where you'll board the cable car that crosses the Tingo canyon with dizzying views, followed by a short walk to the citadel's entrance. Inside the complex, the guide explains the defensive system of walls up to 19 meters high, the more than 400 circular structures, and the geometric friezes that decorate Chachapoya architecture. The day includes lunch in Nuevo Tingo before heading back to Chachapoyas.

Kuélap fortress: walls up to 19 m high and more than 400 circular structures

tours.title: Gocta Waterfall Full Day
tours.shortDescription: A cloud forest hike from Cocachimba to the base of one of the world's tallest waterfalls.
tours.description: A full day of moderate trekking to Gocta Waterfall, a 771-meter cascade split into two drops, ranking among the tallest in the world and unknown to the international scientific community until 2002. The route begins in the village of Cocachimba, at 1,800 meters above sea level, and follows a 5.5-km trail through cloud forest and orchids, with a chance to spot the Andean cock-of-the-rock, all the way to the base of the lower falls. The return follows the same path, with the option to cover the final stretch on horseback, and the day wraps up with a traditional lunch in Cocachimba before heading back to Chachapoyas.

tours.title: Chachapoyas 3D/2N: Kuélap and Gocta
tours.shortDescription: Discover the pre-Inca fortress of Kuélap and the towering Gocta Waterfall on a 3-day trip through Amazonas, with cable car access, a guided hike, and Chachapoyas as your fixed base.
tours.description: This 3-day, 2-night program combines the two great icons of the Amazonas region: the monumental fortress of Kuélap, built in stone by the Chachapoyas culture above 3,000 meters and reached by cable car, and Gocta Waterfall, one of the tallest cascades in the world, with a 771-meter drop split into two falls. Chachapoyas serves as the base of operations throughout the trip, with daily departures to each attraction and a return to the city each night. It's an itinerary designed for travelers seeking history, archaeology, and nature in a short, well-organized format, with moderately difficult hikes and cloud forest scenery.

Gocta Waterfall (771 m), one of the tallest in the world

Fixed base in Chachapoyas, no hotel changes

Admission to the Kuélap Archaeological Complex
Professional Spanish-speaking guide during the Kuélap and Gocta visits

details: Approximate schedule: reception based on flight/bus arrival time, with direct transfer to the hotel.
Free afternoon to acclimatize to the city's altitude of 2,335 meters above sea level.

itinerary.title: Kuélap fortress by cable car
itinerary.description: A full day dedicated to Kuélap, the stone citadel built by the Chachapoyas culture between the 9th and 16th centuries atop a ridge at 3,000 meters above sea level. After a roughly one-hour transfer to the Nuevo Tingo station, board the cable car (about 20 minutes with views of the Tingo river canyon) and walk close to 40 minutes to the fortress entrance, where the guide explains the more than 400 circular structures and the perimeter walls up to 19 meters high.
details: Approximate schedule: pickup at 08:00, cable car at 09:30, fortress entry at 10:30.
Guided visit of 2 to 3 hours inside the archaeological complex.
Return to Chachapoyas: approximately 17:00.

itinerary.title: Gocta Waterfall and departure
itinerary.description: Transfer to the village of Cocachimba, the starting point for the hike to Gocta Waterfall, a 771-meter cascade split into two drops and ranked among the tallest in the world. The moderately difficult trail passes through cloud forest dotted with orchids before reaching the base of the lower drop. After returning to Cocachimba and lunch (optional), a final transfer takes you to Chachapoyas for departure to the airport or bus terminal.
details: Approximate schedule: departure from Chachapoyas at 07:30, hike begins in Cocachimba at 08:30.
Moderately difficult hike, approximately 5.5 km each way (2 to 3 hours per leg).
Departure transfer from Chachapoyas according to flight or bus schedule (afternoon).

tours.title: Historic Center of Lima + Catacombs
tours.shortDescription: A walking tour of the Plaza Mayor, Government Palace, Cathedral, and Plaza San Martín, with a guided visit to the catacombs of the San Francisco Convent.
tours.description: A half day designed to help you understand Lima's colonial origins, founded in 1535 and declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The tour combines the Plaza Mayor with its carved colonial balconies, the exterior of the Government Palace and the Cathedral, and the lively early-20th-century Plaza San Martín, then closes with the circuit's most unusual stop: the catacombs of the San Francisco Convent, where the remains of more than 25,000 people lie arranged in geometric patterns. An ideal first taste of Lima for travelers who have just arrived or are in transit.

The exterior of the Government Palace, with a chance to see the changing of the guard (12:00 noon, only if the tour timing coincides)
Lima Cathedral and the San Francisco square
The catacombs of the San Francisco Convent: more than 25,000 remains in underground galleries
Plaza San Martín, one of the best-preserved republican-era plazas in South America
A guide specialized in Lima's colonial and republican history

Professional bilingual or Spanish-speaking guide

itinerary.title: Pickup in modern Lima
itinerary.description: Meet your guide for pickup at hotels in Miraflores, San Isidro, or Barranco. Transfer by tourist vehicle to Lima's Historic Center, crossing the main avenues that connect modern Lima with the colonial old town.

Journey of roughly 25 to 35 minutes depending on traffic.

itinerary.title: Plaza Mayor of Lima
itinerary.description: Arrival at the Plaza Mayor, the founding heart of the city, laid out in 1535 by Francisco Pizarro. Your guide explains the plaza's history and points out its landmark buildings: the Cathedral, the Government Palace, the Archbishop's Palace, and Lima's City Hall, all featuring the characteristic carved wooden colonial balconies.
details: Walking tour around the plaza's perimeter, approx. 30 minutes.
If timing allows (around midday), you may catch the changing of the guard in front of the Government Palace.
A great spot for panoramic photos of the Cathedral's façade.

itinerary.title: Lima Cathedral and colonial streets
itinerary.description: An exterior view of Lima Cathedral, built on the original 16th-century site, followed by a walk through nearby colonial streets, taking in balconies, historic mansions, and traditional shops in the historic center on the way to the San Francisco square.
details: Entry inside the Cathedral only if included in your tour package (separate admission with most operators).
Walking distance to San Francisco: about 4 to 5 blocks.
An area with heavy street-vendor and pedestrian traffic.

itinerary.title: San Francisco Convent and Catacombs
itinerary.description: A guided visit to the San Francisco Convent, opened in 1672 and famous for its cloister with Sevillian tiles, its historic library, and its striking spiral dome. The tour then descends into the catacombs, a colonial-era underground cemetery used until 1821, where the remains of an estimated 25,000-plus people rest, many bones arranged in geometric patterns by Franciscan friars.
details: Guided visit length: approximately 45 minutes.
Photography is not allowed inside the convent or the catacombs.
Narrow passageways with steps; not recommended for those with severe claustrophobia or limited mobility.

itinerary.title: Plaza San Martín
itinerary.description: A walk to Plaza San Martín, opened in 1921 for the centennial of Peru's independence and surrounded by neoclassical and art deco buildings such as the Gran Hotel Bolívar. Your guide shares the republican-era history tied to the plaza and its equestrian statue of José de San Martín.
details: Distance from San Francisco to the plaza: about 6 to 7 blocks, covered by vehicle or on foot depending on the group's pace.
A reference point connecting to Jirón de la Unión, a pedestrian shopping street.
A good moment for any final questions for your guide about Lima's history.

itinerary.title: Return to the starting point
itinerary.description: Transfer back to your hotel or meeting point in Miraflores, San Isidro, or Barranco, where the service ends. The rest of the day is free to keep exploring independently or to combine with another afternoon tour.
details: Approximate end time: 12:30 to 1:00 PM depending on traffic.
An afternoon option is available starting at 2:00 PM for those who prefer that time slot.
Bring water and sunscreen for the full tour.

tours.title: Lima City Tour + Museo Larco
tours.shortDescription: A tour through Miraflores and San Isidro with a view of Huaca Pucllana, plus a guided visit to Museo Larco, one of the world's finest collections of pre-Columbian art.
tours.description: A city tour designed as a first introduction to Lima, and to 5,000 years of Peruvian history, in a single morning or afternoon. The route passes the lookout points of the Costa Verde and the modern districts of Miraflores and San Isidro, with a view of the adobe pyramid of Huaca Pucllana right in the middle of the city, before arriving at Museo Larco. Housed in an 18th-century viceregal mansion, the museum is internationally renowned for its collection of ceramics, textiles, gold, and silver, along with its celebrated gallery of Moche erotic art. Ideal for first-time visitors to Lima or those with a same-day connection.
highlights: Miraflores and its lookout points over the Costa Verde and the Pacific Ocean
San Isidro and the elegant El Olivar Forest
A panoramic view of Huaca Pucllana, a pre-Inca pyramid in the middle of the city
Museo Larco: a collection of pre-Columbian gold, silver, textiles, and ceramics
The Moche erotic art gallery, one of the museum's most visited spaces
The museum's colonial gardens, perfect for photos to close out the tour

Small or shared groups depending on the operator.
Keep your voucher or booking confirmation handy.

itinerary.title: Miraflores and the Costa Verde
itinerary.description: A panoramic tour of Miraflores, with photo stops at the Parque del Amor (Park of Love) and the cliffs above the Costa Verde. Your guide explains Lima's modern urban development and its contrast with the colonial layout of the historic center.
details: Short stop at Parque del Amor or the Miraflores boardwalk, approx. 15 minutes.
A great spot for photos of the coastline and the paragliders soaring above it.
An area with cafés and shops if you'd like some extra free time.

itinerary.title: San Isidro and Huaca Pucllana
itinerary.description: Transfer to San Isidro, a residential and financial district known for the El Olivar Forest, with a photo stop at the exterior of Huaca Pucllana, an adobe and clay pyramid built by the Lima culture more than 1,500 years ago, now surrounded by modern buildings in Miraflores.
details: Exterior view of Huaca Pucllana; entry to the archaeological site is not included in this package.
A night visit to Pucllana can be added as a separate activity.
Photo stop of approximately 15 to 20 minutes.

itinerary.title: Museo Larco: pre-Columbian collections
itinerary.description: Entry to Museo Larco, housed in an 18th-century viceregal mansion built atop a pre-Inca pyramid. A guided visit through the main galleries, featuring Moche and Chimú ceramics, the gold and silver room, and textiles considered among the finest in the Andean world.
details: Approximate entry time: 11:00 AM, with a guided visit lasting 60 to 75 minutes.
The museum holds more than 45,000 pieces in its collection, a portion of which is on display.
Museum shop available at the end of the visit.

itinerary.title: Erotic art gallery and gardens
itinerary.description: A visit to the museum's famous gallery of Moche erotic ceramics, one of its most talked-about collections for the light it sheds on daily life and beliefs in ancient Peru. The tour closes in the museum's colonial gardens, filled with bougainvillea, with a café overlooking the courtyard.

The gardens are ideal for final photos and wrapping up the tour.
A short bit of free time before heading back, approx. 10 to 15 minutes.

details: Approximate end time: 1:15 to 1:45 PM depending on traffic and destination.

tours.title: Pachacámac + Museo Larco
tours.shortDescription: A full-day archaeological route to the Sanctuary of Pachacámac, the most important ceremonial center of the pre-Hispanic central coast, combined with Museo Larco.
tours.description: A full-day tour for travelers interested in Peru's ancient history. The morning is spent at the Pachacámac Archaeological Sanctuary in the Lurín Valley, a pilgrimage center in continuous use for more than 1,200 years that brings together structures built by the Lima, Wari, Ychsma, and Inca cultures, including the Temple of the Sun and the Acllahuasi. After a lunch break, the afternoon continues at Museo Larco, with its collection of pre-Columbian ceramics, gold, and textiles, rounding out a day devoted entirely to understanding the cultural continuity of ancient Peru, from the pre-Inca societies through the arrival of the Incas.

The Temple of the Sun, built by the Incas atop the highest point of the complex

Pachacámac's site museum, home to the original idol of the god Pachacámac

itinerary.title: Departure from Lima to the Lurín Valley
itinerary.description: Hotel pickup and departure south of Lima via the Panamericana Sur highway, passing through the districts of Chorrillos and Villa El Salvador before reaching the Lurín Valley, home to the sanctuary. Your guide introduces the site's historical background along the way.

itinerary.title: Pachacámac site museum

Starting point for the walking tour of the archaeological complex.

itinerary.title: Touring the sanctuary: Temple of the Sun and Acllahuasi
itinerary.description: A walk through the archaeological circuit, including the Temple of the Sun, built by the Incas at the highest point of the complex with views over the Pacific, the Acllahuasi, or Palace of the Chosen Women, and the terraced plazas and temples of the pre-Inca cultures that occupied the valley before the Inca conquest.
details: Walking circuit of approximately 1.5 to 2 km over desert, uneven terrain.
Comfortable footwear, a cap, sunscreen, and water are recommended.
Panoramic views of the coastline and the Lurín Valley from the Temple of the Sun.

itinerary.title: Return to Lima and lunch break

A stroll through the museum's colonial gardens at the end of the visit.
Museum shop and café available.

itinerary.title: Return to the starting point

details: Approximate end time: 5:00 to 5:30 PM depending on traffic.
Bring a camera with a good zoom for the panoramic views at Pachacámac.
Ask the operator about swapping the order of the visits depending on the day's availability.

tours.title: Palomino Islands and Swimming with Sea Lions
tours.shortDescription: A yacht trip from Callao to the Palomino Islands to swim with a wild sea lion colony and spot guano birds and Humboldt penguins.
tours.description: A marine adventure just minutes from Lima. The boat departs from the Muelle de Guerra (Naval Pier) at Plaza Grau in Callao and sails past San Lorenzo, El Frontón, and Cavinzas islands, where you may spot Humboldt penguins, sea lions, and a wide variety of guano birds, before reaching the Palomino Islands. There, in a wetsuit and under the crew's guidance, passengers can get into the water to swim near a wild colony of several hundred sea lions in their natural habitat, a rare experience so close to a South American capital.
highlights: Yacht departure from the historic Muelle de Guerra (Naval Pier) at Plaza Grau, Callao
Views of San Lorenzo Island and the former El Frontón prison
A wild colony of several hundred sea lions on the Palomino Islands
Optional swim with sea lions in a wetsuit
Possible sightings of Humboldt penguins and guano birds
Safety briefing and equipment provided by the crew

Wetsuit for swimming with the sea lions

itinerary.title: Meeting point at Plaza Grau, Callao

Bring a valid ID; boarding checks may apply.
Wear a swimsuit under your clothes, and bring a towel, cap, and sunscreen.

itinerary.title: Departure and sailing through Callao Bay
itinerary.description: Departure from Callao with views of the port's historic buildings, San Lorenzo Island (the largest off the coast of Lima), and the El Frontón islet, once home to an old prison. Your guide explains the area's naval and port history along the way.
details: Approximately 45 minutes to 1 hour of sailing before reaching the islands.
Moderate swells possible offshore; best suited for those who don't get seasick easily.
A great stretch for photos of the bay and Callao's skyline.

itinerary.title: Wildlife watching: guano birds and Humboldt penguins
itinerary.description: Sailing along the Cavinzas Islands and surroundings, spotting guano birds such as boobies and guanay cormorants, with a chance to see Humboldt penguins on the rocks near shore, as well as sea lions resting on the rock formations.
details: Observation from the boat, with no landing.
A zoom camera or binoculars are recommended for a better view.
Penguin sightings depend on the season and are not guaranteed.

itinerary.title: Arrival at the Palomino Islands and swim with sea lions
itinerary.description: Arrival at the Palomino Islands, home to a wild colony of several hundred sea lions. In wetsuits and under crew supervision, passengers who wish to can get into the water to swim near the sea lions, curious, generally non-aggressive animals in their own habitat.
details: Time in the water: approximately 30 to 40 minutes.
The activity is optional; those who prefer not to swim can watch from the boat.

itinerary.title: Return to Callao
itinerary.description: The return trip begins, sailing once more past cliffs and islets, with one last chance for photos of the marine wildlife and coastal scenery before reaching the pier.

Restrooms and showers available at the pier or nearby facilities, depending on the operator.

tours.title: Moche and Chimú Route: Huacas del Sol y la Luna, Chan Chan, and Huanchaco
tours.shortDescription: A complete archaeological tour of the Moche temples, the Chan Chan citadel, and the traditional beach town of Huanchaco.
tours.description: One of the best cultural routes in northern Peru. The tour combines the visual power of Huaca de la Luna, with its polychrome murals and Moche worldview, the sheer scale of Chan Chan, the Chimú capital and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and a coastal finish in Huanchaco, where totora reed boats and the fishing traditions of the northern coast still survive. itinerary.title: Pickup in Trujillo and departure to the Moche Valley
itinerary.description: Meet your guide at your hotel or a central point near Trujillo's Plaza de Armas. Departure by tourist vehicle to the Moche countryside, about 15 minutes from the city, passing farmland of sugarcane and corn still irrigated in part by the ancient Moche hydraulic system.
details: Approximate pickup window: 9:00 to 9:15 AM, depending on your hotel's location.
Bring a valid ID and sunscreen; most of the tour is outdoors.

itinerary.title: Huacas de Moche Site Museum
itinerary.description: A visit to the site museum before entering the huaca, where original pieces recovered from the excavations are on display: ceremonial ceramics, textiles, copper tools, and panels explaining the social and religious organization of the Moche culture (1st-9th centuries AD).
details: Complex hours: Tuesday to Sunday, 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, last entry to the huaca at 3:30 PM.
The museum sets the context for what you'll see at the huaca; visit lasts 20 to 25 minutes.
Closed Mondays; the operator will rearrange the day's order if needed.

itinerary.title: Huaca de la Luna
itinerary.description: A guided climb through the stacked platforms of Huaca de la Luna, a Moche ceremonial center built and rebuilt over itself several times. The tour showcases the best-preserved polychrome murals on the northern coast, with the repeated image of the god Ai Apaec, or 'the Decapitator,' and explains the evidence of human sacrifice found in the Ceremonial Plaza.
details: Guided visit of 45 to 60 minutes across ramps and terraced plazas; uneven ground in places.
The adjoining Huaca del Sol (Temple of the Sun) is viewed from outside lookout points (the interior is closed to visitors, still under study).

itinerary.title: Tschudi Citadel, Chan Chan
itinerary.description: A transfer of about 20 minutes to the Chan Chan complex, capital of the Chimú kingdom and the largest adobe citadel in pre-Hispanic America, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986. A tour of the Nik-An sector (formerly called Tschudi), the only one of the nine citadels open to the public, with its Ceremonial Plaza, the Audience Hall, storerooms, and ceremonial well, decorated with geometric reliefs of fish, seabirds, and fishing nets molded in clay.
details: About a 20-minute drive between Moche and the Chan Chan sector; a marked walking circuit of approximately 1 km.
The friezes reflect the Chimú connection to the sea, the foundation of their economy and worldview (12th-15th centuries).
A cap, water, and comfortable footwear are recommended for the direct midday sun.

itinerary.title: Huanchaco: lunch by the sea
itinerary.description: Transfer to Huanchaco, a beach town and fishing cove 15 minutes from Chan Chan. Free time for lunch at one of the restaurants along the boardwalk, with specialties like ceviche and sudado de pescado (Peruvian fish stew), while watching the totora reed boats come and go along the shore.
details: Suggested free time: 60 to 75 minutes; lunch not included except in special packages.
Totora reed boats are pre-Hispanic vessels still used by local fishermen today.

itinerary.title: Huanchaco boardwalk and pier
itinerary.description: A stroll along Huanchaco's boardwalk and wooden pier, with time for photos, shopping for totora fiber handicrafts, and a panoramic view of Huanchaco's colonial church atop the rocky headland.
details: The pier offers the best overall view of the beach and the totora boats lined up on the sand.
An area with craft shops, ice cream parlors, and traditional cevicherías.

itinerary.title: Return to Trujillo
itinerary.description: Final transfer back to your hotel or meeting point in downtown Trujillo, bringing the day's service to a close.
details: Approximate arrival time in Trujillo: 5:15 to 5:30 PM, depending on traffic.
Coordinate with your guide if you'd like to be dropped off somewhere other than the pickup point.
The close of a full day on the Moche-Chimú route.

tours.title: El Brujo + Museo Cao and the Lady of Cao from Trujillo
tours.shortDescription: Visit the El Brujo complex and discover the story of the Lady of Cao, one of ancient Peru's most important female rulers.

tours.title: Pómac Forest + Túcume Full Day
tours.shortDescription: Dry forest scenery, endemic birds, and Sicán archaeology on a different route from Chiclayo, away from the usual museum circuit.
tours.description: A full-day experience combining nature and culture on the north coast, perfect for travelers who've already covered the Lambayeque museums and want something different. tours.title: Tumbes Mangroves + Puerto Pizarro Full Day

From Tumbes, you're taken to the bay of Puerto Pizarro, a fishing cove and gateway to the Tumbes Mangroves National Sanctuary, where you board a traditional boat to explore the estuaries between mangroves that reach up to 6 meters tall. tours.title: Oxapampa, Pozuzo and Villa Rica 3D/2N

tours.title: Yanachaga-Chemillén National Park: San Alberto Sector
tours.shortDescription: A full day of hiking in the San Alberto sector of Yanachaga-Chemillén National Park, with cloud forest, orchids, and birdwatching just minutes from Oxapampa.
tours.description: The San Alberto sector is the most accessible gateway into Yanachaga-Chemillén National Park, just 5.5 km from Oxapampa, blending high jungle and humid grassland between 2,200 and 3,200 meters in elevation. The day follows the El Cedro trail through dense cloud forest and the Orchid Trail, home to dozens of orchid, bromeliad, and fern species growing alongside towering cedar trees. This is a plan built for nature travelers looking for a real day of hiking, away from Selva Central's more crowded circuits.

tours.title: Wari, Quinua and Pampa de Ayacucho

tours.title: Santa Bárbara Mine + Sacsamarca from Huancavelica
tours.shortDescription: A historic half day to the colonial Santa Bárbara Mercury Mine, the most important in the Spanish empire in South America, and the picturesque stone village of Sacsamarca.
tours.description: A journey through one of the most intense chapters of Peru's colonial history. Discovered in 1564, the Santa Bárbara Mine was, for a century and a half, the world's largest mercury deposit and the key resource that sustained silver extraction in Potosí, earning it the nickname "jewel of the Spanish crown." The tour first visits Sacsamarca, a stone village declared a National Cultural Heritage Site whose first inhabitants were miners forced to work at Santa Bárbara, then continues to the mine's remains: the colonial entrance gate, the church dedicated to the patron saint of miners, old smelting furnaces and abandoned houses at 3,900 meters above sea level.

tours.description: An off-the-beaten-path route that combines geology and archaeology a short distance from Huancavelica. tours.title: Manu Cultural Zone 4D/3N from Cusco
