itinerary.title: Iquitos - Nauta - entry via Yanayacu-Pucate
itinerary.description: Transfer to Nauta and a boat ride along the Marañón River to the reserve's entry ranger station, where you'll complete official registration. Travel continues along the Yanayacu-Pucate basin to the first camp, with riverside birdwatching and a first taste of flooded forest during the afternoon journey.
details: Approximate schedule: pickup 6:00 AM, arrival in Nauta 7:30 AM, about 4-hour boat ride.
Entry registration at the SERNANP ranger station (ID required).
Setting up camp before nightfall.

itinerary.title: Traveling to Pato Cocha
itinerary.description: A day of travel deeper into the reserve, stopping at Pato Cocha, a lake with a wide variety of water birds, caimans, and frequent pink river dolphin sightings. A short interpretive walk on the shore introduces flora typical of flooded forest, such as aguaje and renaco.
details: Approximate schedule: departure 6:30 AM, arrival at Pato Cocha around midday.
Wildlife watching by silent canoe during the afternoon.
Short interpretive walk, 45 minutes to 1 hour, depending on water level.

itinerary.title: Arrival at Cocha El Dorado and Canta Gallo shelter
itinerary.description: Continued travel into the heart of the reserve, arriving at Cocha El Dorado, Pacaya-Samiria's signature lake, known for pink river dolphin sightings and, occasionally, Amazonian manatees. Camp for this night and the next is set up at the Canta Gallo shelter, on the lake's shore.
details: Approximate schedule: morning travel, arrival at Cocha El Dorado before lunch.
Afternoon dedicated to wildlife watching on the lake by canoe.
Clear night skies ideal for stargazing, far from artificial light.

itinerary.title: Cocha El Dorado: canoe, walk and traditional fishing
itinerary.description: A full day at Cocha El Dorado. In the morning, a tour by traditional boat and canoe through different parts of the lake. During the dry season (June to November), an interpretive walk around the lake is added to spot wildlife and flora from land. In the afternoon, traditional fishing for piranha and peacock bass, followed after dinner by a nighttime outing in search of caimans by flashlight.
details: Approximate schedule: canoe travel 7:00 to 11:00 AM.
Interpretive walk (dry season only): 3:00 to 4:30 PM.
Traditional fishing before dinner; caiman spotting after 8:00 PM.

itinerary.title: A final dawn in the reserve and return to Iquitos
itinerary.description: An early departure for one last wildlife-watching trip before breaking camp. The return journey follows the Yanayacu-Pucate basin to the exit ranger station, then on to Nauta and Iquitos by road, with arrival at your hotel expected in the late afternoon.
details: Approximate schedule: wildlife-watching outing 5:30 AM, breakfast and breaking camp 8:00 AM.
Return river journey to Nauta: approximately 5 hours.
Estimated arrival at your hotel in Iquitos: 6:00 to 7:00 PM.

researchSources: SERNANP Pacaya Samiria Cocha El Dorado

tours.title: Tambopata Complete: Lake Sandoval + Chuncho Clay Lick 5D/4N
tours.shortDescription: The most complete Amazon program in our catalog: five days to explore Lake Sandoval and travel upriver to the Chuncho clay lick, combining two of the most iconic experiences in the Tambopata National Reserve with extra time for observation at each.
tours.description: This five-day program brings together, in a single route, the two signature experiences of the Tambopata National Reserve: Lake Sandoval, with its giant river otter families and palm swamps, and the Chuncho clay lick, one of the Amazon's largest macaw feeding sites. Unlike shorter programs, it dedicates a full day to each area — including a full day of river travel between the two zones along the Madre de Dios and Tambopata rivers — allowing for longer observation sessions, better odds of sightings, and extra time for walks, canoeing, and nighttime activities. This is the recommended choice for travelers who want to experience the southern Peruvian Amazon in depth, without rushing through either of its two great attractions.
highlights: Lake Sandoval and the Chuncho clay lick in a single program, with more time at each site
Travel along two rivers: Madre de Dios and Tambopata
An extended paddle-boat session on Lake Sandoval in search of giant river otters
A full sunrise session at the Chuncho clay lick watching macaws and parrots
Three nighttime wildlife excursions over the course of the trip
The most immersive Amazon program in our catalog, ideal for photographers and birdwatchers
includes: Airport/bus terminal - river ports - airport/bus terminal transfers
Round-trip river travel on the Madre de Dios and Tambopata rivers
4 nights' accommodation at Amazon lodges
Meals per itinerary (lunch and dinner day 1; full board days 2 through 4; breakfast day 5)
Guided walk and paddle-boat ride on Lake Sandoval
Entrance and guided visit to the Chuncho clay lick
Nighttime wildlife-spotting excursions
Canoeing or piranha fishing activity
Spanish-speaking naturalist guide throughout the trip
excludes: Flights or ground transportation to/from Puerto Maldonado
Breakfast on day 1 (depending on flight arrival time)
Specialized photography equipment (telephoto lenses, tripods, etc.)
Services not specified in the program

itinerary.title: Puerto Maldonado and the journey to the Sandoval sector
itinerary.description: Pickup in Puerto Maldonado and transfer to the port on the Madre de Dios River for the trip's first boat ride, about 40 minutes, to the lodge in the Lake Sandoval sector of the Tambopata National Reserve. After check-in, an interpretive walk along trails near the lodge, and once night falls, the first of the trip's three nighttime excursions in search of caimans.
details: Approximate schedule: pickup 6:00-10:00 AM depending on flight, 40-minute boat ride, arrival at the lodge between 11:00 AM and 1:00 PM.
2-hour interpretive walk through secondary forest and palm swamp.
Nighttime boat excursion from 7:00 PM (~1 hour) in search of caimans.

itinerary.title: A full day at Lake Sandoval
itinerary.description: Unlike the shorter programs, this day is dedicated entirely to Lake Sandoval, with a longer paddle-boat session that covers different areas of the lake to maximize the chances of encountering the giant river otter families that live in its waters. The 3 km walk to the lakeshore, a boxed breakfast, and lunch back at the lodge are paired with an afternoon at the observation tower and a talk on the ecology of Amazonian oxbow lakes.
details: Approximate schedule: departure 5:30 AM with coffee, 3 km walk (~1 hour), extended paddle-boat ride of 2.5 to 3 hours.
Boxed breakfast during the excursion; return to the lodge and lunch at 1:30 PM.
Afternoon: observation tower, interpretive talk on Amazonian oxbow lakes, and free time.

itinerary.title: River transfer: from the Sandoval sector to the Tambopata River
itinerary.description: A transition day between the trip's two main zones. In the morning, a return boat ride to the port in Puerto Maldonado, followed by a ground transfer to the port on the Tambopata River, where you'll begin a 1.5- to 2-hour upriver journey to a lodge in a more remote sector of the reserve, near the Chuncho clay lick. In the afternoon, a short orientation walk, and after dinner, the trip's second nighttime excursion.
details: Approximate schedule: breakfast 7:00 AM, return boat ride to Puerto Maldonado ~40 minutes.
Ground transfer ~30-45 minutes to the Tambopata River port; upriver travel 1.5 to 2 hours.
Short orientation walk on arrival and nighttime excursion from 7:30 PM (~1.5 hours).

itinerary.title: Chuncho clay lick: sunrise with the macaws
itinerary.description: The high point of the trip. Wake up before dawn to travel to the viewing post facing the Chuncho clay lick, where macaws, parrots, and parakeets gather to feed on the mineral clay as soon as the sun rises. The viewing session, longer than on the four-day program, allows time to take in different species and their arrival patterns. In the afternoon, an optional canoeing or piranha-fishing activity and a farewell dinner recapping the species spotted throughout the trip.
details: Approximate schedule: wake-up 4:30 AM, boat ride at 5:00 AM (~30-45 minutes) to the viewing post.
Clay lick activity: roughly 6:00-10:30/11:00 AM, with a boxed breakfast during the wait.
Afternoon: canoeing/kayaking or piranha fishing, and a farewell dinner recapping the wildlife spotted.
itinerary.distance: ~30-45 min boat ride + ~4-5 hour viewing session

itinerary.title: Return to Puerto Maldonado
itinerary.description: A final morning in the rainforest and breakfast before the downriver return trip on the Tambopata River. Ground transfer to Puerto Maldonado, with a brief stop at the local market, and a final transfer to the airport or bus terminal.
details: Approximate schedule: breakfast 6:30 AM, departure from the lodge 7:00 AM.
Downriver return trip: approximately 1 to 1.5 hours.
Final ground transfer with a 20-minute stop at the local market before the airport/terminal.

tours.title: Bahuaja-Sonene Amazon Expedition 5D/4N
tours.shortDescription: A specialized five-day expedition from Puerto Maldonado to Bahuaja-Sonene National Park, on the border with Bolivia, to discover the Heath Pampas, Peru's only tropical wet savanna.
tours.description: Bahuaja-Sonene is one of the least-visited and most distinctive Amazon destinations in southern Peru: a national park that protects both humid rainforest and the Heath Pampas, the country's only tropical wet savanna, home to species found nowhere else in Peru, such as the maned wolf and the pampas deer. This five-day expedition departs from Puerto Maldonado and navigates the Madre de Dios and Heath rivers to the border with Bolivia, checking in at the Puerto Pardo ranger checkpoint before entering the park. The program combines macaw-watching at natural clay licks, walks through gallery forest and savanna, and a cultural encounter with the native Ese'Eja community of Sonene, in a specialized operation that requires advance coordination and permits depending on the point of entry.
tours.location: Madre de Dios / Puno / Bahuaja-Sonene-Tambopata Landscape
highlights: Heath Pampas: Peru's only tropical wet savanna
River travel along the Madre de Dios and Heath rivers to the border with Bolivia
Macaw and parrot clay lick on the Heath River
Cultural encounter with the native Ese'Eja community of Sonene
Chance of spotting rare wildlife such as the maned wolf and pampas deer
Specialized expedition into a restricted-access, permit-controlled area
includes: Pickup at the Puerto Maldonado airport or bus terminal
River transport on the Madre de Dios and Heath rivers
Check-in and permit coordination at the SERNANP checkpoint
4 nights' accommodation at an authorized lodge or campsite in the area
Full board during the expedition (from lunch on day 1 through breakfast on day 5)
Bilingual naturalist guide specialized in savanna and rainforest wildlife
River equipment and life jackets
excludes: Domestic or international flights to/from Puerto Maldonado
Tips for the guide and camp staff
Optional activities not mentioned in the itinerary

itinerary.title: Puerto Maldonado and river travel on the Madre de Dios and Heath rivers
itinerary.description: Arrival in Puerto Maldonado, the capital of Madre de Dios, with a brief tour of the town and its waterfront promenade along the Madre de Dios River. In the afternoon, board a motorized boat to navigate the Madre de Dios River and head up the Heath River, the natural border with Bolivia, toward the edges of Bahuaja-Sonene National Park. Along the way, mandatory check-in at the Puerto Pardo (SERNANP) ranger checkpoint.
details: Pickup at the Puerto Maldonado airport/terminal and transfer to the river port
River travel on the Madre de Dios and Heath rivers (approx. 4 h)
Check-in at the SERNANP ranger checkpoint in Puerto Pardo, on the border with Bolivia

itinerary.title: Macaw clay lick on the Heath River and first entry into the Heath Pampas
itinerary.description: At dawn, navigate to a macaw and parrot clay lick on the banks of the Heath River, one of the most striking displays of color in the southern Amazon. After breakfast, an ethnobotanical walk reveals the traditional uses of rainforest plants, and in the afternoon you'll enter the Heath Pampas for the first time — Peru's only tropical wet savanna, a grassland ecosystem surrounded by Amazon rainforest.
details: Approx. 5:30-7:00 am: watching macaws and parrots at the Heath River clay lick
Guided ethnobotanical walk through the riverside forest
Afternoon: on-foot entry into the Heath Pampas in search of savanna birds and signs of pampas deer

itinerary.title: Exploring the Heath Pampas and the Ese'Eja community of Sonene
itinerary.description: A full day exploring the Heath Pampas and its surrounding gallery forests, a unique habitat where, with patience and a bit of luck, you may find signs of maned wolf or pampas deer — species found nowhere else in Peru. In the afternoon, visit the native Ese'Eja community of Sonene, where residents share their ancestral relationship with the forest, fishing, and traditional crafts.
details: Morning: extended walk across the pampas and adjacent gallery forests
Watching typical savanna wildlife: birds of prey, herons, and possible maned wolf tracks
Afternoon: visit and cultural exchange with the Ese'Eja community of Sonene

itinerary.title: Hidden forest trails and wildlife watching
itinerary.description: Explore little-used trails through the primary forest surrounding the pampas, in search of primates, toucans, and, overhead, possible sightings of the harpy eagle, one of the Amazon's most iconic predators. At nightfall, a night boat excursion along the Heath River, lighting up the banks in search of caimans and nocturnal birds, before enjoying the last night deep in the rainforest.
details: Morning: walk through primary forest trails in search of primates and birds
Free afternoon for landscape photography and rest at camp
Night: night safari by boat along the Heath River
itinerary.distance: Walking and night river travel, approx. 4 h

itinerary.title: Return to Puerto Maldonado
itinerary.description: After breakfast, begin the descent down the Heath and Madre de Dios rivers back to Puerto Maldonado, closing out an expedition that combines classic Amazon rainforest with the unique savanna landscape of Peru's far south. Final transfer to the airport or bus terminal according to the traveler's departure schedule.
details: Breakfast and early check-out from the base camp
River travel back down the Heath and Madre de Dios rivers (approx. 4-5 h)
Final transfer to the Puerto Maldonado airport/terminal

tours.title: Allpahuayo-Mishana National Reserve Full Day from Iquitos
tours.shortDescription: A one-day excursion to white-sand forests (varillales) and the blackwater Nanay River, less than an hour from Iquitos.
tours.description: A full day of nature exploration in Allpahuayo-Mishana National Reserve, located between kilometers 25 and 28 of the Iquitos-Nauta highway. It protects a unique sample of varillales — forests growing on low-fertility white sand that shelter endemic species like the Iquitos gnatcatcher — along with forests flooded by the blackwaters of the Nanay River. The route combines interpretive trails and birdwatching with an easy walk, ideal for travelers with limited time in Loreto who still want to experience an Amazon ecosystem quite different from the whitewater rivers and oxbow lakes. It's a low-difficulty outing, highly recommended for birdwatchers and nature photographers.
highlights: White-sand forests (varillales), unique to the Amazon
Chance to spot the Iquitos gnatcatcher, an endemic bird of the reserve
Allpahuayo Research Center (IIAP) and its interpretive trails
Blackwater flooded forests along the Nanay River
Birdwatching circuit near kilometer 25
Less than an hour from Iquitos — ideal for a short outing
includes: Pickup and drop-off at a centrally located Iquitos hotel
Tourist transport along the Iquitos-Nauta highway
Local naturalist guide
Entry to Allpahuayo-Mishana National Reserve
Interpretive walk along the reserve's trails
excludes: Lunch (a box lunch can be arranged for an extra cost)
Binoculars (bringing your own is recommended for birdwatching)

itinerary.title: Pickup at hotel in Iquitos
itinerary.description: Pickup at your hotel in Iquitos with an early departure, key to making the most of the hours of peak bird activity in the forest. The guide gives an introduction to the varillal ecosystem you'll visit during the day.
details: Departure recommended before 6:30 am, when wildlife activity is highest.
Wear long sleeves, bring insect repellent, and comfortable shoes for walking on sand.
Bringing your own binoculars is recommended.

itinerary.title: Drive along the Iquitos-Nauta highway
itinerary.description: The vehicle heads south on the Iquitos-Nauta highway, the only paved road out of Iquitos, entering the boundaries of Allpahuayo-Mishana National Reserve around kilometer 25.
details: Iquitos to the reserve: approximately 25 km / 30-45 minutes.
The reserve protects nearly 58,000 hectares of white-sand forest and blackwater habitat.
Check-in at the reserve's ranger checkpoint.

itinerary.title: Birdwatching circuit (km 25)
itinerary.description: On the birdwatching circuit near km 25, walk slowly along a trail through the varillal, habitat of endemic species such as the Iquitos gnatcatcher (Polioptila clementsi), only described in 2005 and found nowhere else on Earth.
details: The reserve has 475 recorded bird species.
Chance to spot the Iquitos gnatcatcher and other varillal species.
Slow-paced walk, ideal for bird photography.

itinerary.title: Allpahuayo Research Center (IIAP)
itinerary.description: Visit the Allpahuayo Research Center (CIA), run by the Peruvian Amazon Research Institute (IIAP), with interpretive trails crossing dry high varillal and wet low varillal, plus a garden of native medicinal and fruit plants.
details: Interpretive trail with panels explaining varillal ecology.
A single walk comparing dry high varillal and wet low varillal.
Display of medicinal and fruit plants used by local communities.

itinerary.title: Blackwater section of the Nanay River
itinerary.description: The route approaches the section where the forest floods with the blackwaters of the Nanay River, stained that color by a high concentration of plant tannins. It's a good time to observe the transition between dry varillal and flooded forest.
details: Blackwaters typical of white-sand soils, highly acidic and low in nutrients.
Visible contrast between high varillal and flooded forest.
Chance to spot amphibians and reptiles typical of this microhabitat.

itinerary.title: Snack break inside the reserve
itinerary.description: A stop for a snack or box lunch inside the reserve, in a covered rest area, before heading back toward Iquitos.
details: Box-lunch-style snack (arrange in advance, additional cost).
Rest area with benches and shade inside the reserve.
Last photos of the varillal before departing.

itinerary.title: Return to Iquitos
itinerary.description: Return along the Iquitos-Nauta highway to the city, arriving at your hotel in the early afternoon, closing out a short but intense outing in one of the most distinctive ecosystems in the Peruvian Amazon.
details: Return to Iquitos: approximately 30-45 minutes.
Estimated arrival at the hotel: 1:15-1:30 pm.
End of tour services.

tours.title: Cordillera Azul Expedition 4D/3N from Tarapoto
tours.shortDescription: A specialized 4-day expedition from Tarapoto into the buffer zone of Cordillera Azul National Park, traveling by 4x4 to the hamlet of Plataforma, with a focus on nature, photography, and observing endemic wildlife.
tours.description: Cordillera Azul National Park protects one of the largest stretches of pristine high jungle left in Peru, but its core zone remains closed to conventional tourism and reserved for scientific research under SERNANP. This 4-day, 3-night expedition does not enter the park's core zone: it operates within its extensive buffer zone, traveling by 4x4 from Tarapoto via Bellavista to the hamlet of Plataforma, the same access route used by international ornithological research expeditions. The program combines observation hikes, environmental interpretation, and nature photography in high-altitude cloud forest, with simple lodging at a community-run lodge. Given the access conditions and terrain, it's aimed at travelers in good physical condition who have realistic expectations about the infrastructure available in one of the country's least-visited protected areas.
tours.location: Tarapoto / Juanjuí / Cordillera Azul buffer zone
highlights: 4x4 access to Plataforma, gateway to the park's buffer zone
High-jungle cloud forest with exceptional biodiversity
An area known for the discovery of endemic species only recently described by science
Focus on nature photography and environmental interpretation
Community-based lodging and low-impact tourism
Route operated on request, ideal for small or private groups
includes: Ground transportation Tarapoto–Bellavista–Plataforma–Tarapoto, including the 4x4 stretch
Local or nature-specialized guide throughout the route
3 nights' lodging at a rustic community lodge in Plataforma
Full board for all 4 days (breakfast, lunch, and dinner, except where noted)
Coordination and permits with the local community in the buffer zone
Ongoing support from the agency
excludes: Specialized photography or field equipment (spotting scopes, telephoto lenses, etc.)
Services not mentioned in the itinerary

itinerary.title: Tarapoto – Bellavista – Plataforma
itinerary.description: Early departure from Tarapoto along the Fernando Belaúnde Terry Highway to Bellavista, the gateway to the buffer zone of Cordillera Azul National Park. From there, continue by 4x4 along a steadily climbing mountain track to the hamlet of Plataforma, already within the buffer zone, crossing a marked altitudinal gradient from premontane forest to cloud forest. The route offers landscape and bird watching right from the road; lodging is at a rustic community lodge with a private bathroom and hot water.
details: Approximate schedule: departure from Tarapoto at 05:30-06:00, arrival in Bellavista at 08:00.
Bellavista–Plataforma stretch by 4x4 on a graded dirt track, approximately 4 to 5 hours.
Settle in at the rustic Plataforma lodge before nightfall.
itinerary.distance: Tarapoto–Plataforma ~140 km (part paved, part dirt track) / 6-7 h

itinerary.title: Exploring the cloud forest in the buffer zone
itinerary.description: A full day of hikes along trails around Plataforma, within the park's buffer zone, in search of Cordillera Azul's extraordinary diversity of wildlife and landscapes: mist-shrouded forests, ravines, and natural viewpoints. The area is internationally recognized for the discovery of endemic species only described by science in recent decades, such as the scarlet-banded barbet (Capito wallacei), so the day combines nature, photography, and environmental interpretation with a specialized guide.
details: Approximate schedule: departure from the lodge at 05:30-06:00 to take advantage of morning wildlife activity.
Hikes along cloud forest trails with moderate to steep elevation changes.
Return to the lodge around midday, with a second outing in the afternoon.

itinerary.title: Second day in the field at altitude
itinerary.description: A second full day in the buffer zone, exploring trails and viewpoints at a different elevation than the day before to broaden the photographic and wildlife record. The pace favors slow, careful observation, ideal for nature photography as well as for spotting hard-to-detect species native to this high-jungle relict forest, one of the least studied and best preserved in Peru. The afternoon is left for landscape photography, time with the local community of Plataforma, and rest.
details: Approximate schedule: departure at 06:00, return for lunch, and a second outing at 15:00.
Route through a different sector than the previous day to diversify sightings.
Conversation with guides and local residents about community forest management.

itinerary.title: Final field outing and return to Tarapoto
itinerary.description: One last early-morning observation outing before heading back. Descend by 4x4 along the same track to Bellavista, then continue on paved road to Tarapoto, with arrival expected in the late afternoon. Due to road conditions, timing can vary with the weather, so it's recommended not to book departure flights on the same day as the return.
details: Approximate schedule: final field outing 05:30-07:30.
Descent from Plataforma to Bellavista by 4x4, approximately 4 to 5 hours.
Arrival in Tarapoto: approximately 17:00-18:00 (approximate, subject to weather and track conditions).

tours.title: Santa Cruz Trek in Huascarán National Park 4D/3N
tours.location: Huaraz / Cordillera Blanca / Huascarán National Park

hotelAddOn.note: Opcional para noches pre/post en Huaraz. En la ruta Santa Cruz las noches principales son en campamento; validar distribución final con asesor.

internalNotes.pricingUse: Precio referencial de tour base sin alojamiento. Validar tarifa final con operador local, ingresos, temporada, comisiones y disponibilidad antes de confirmar.

tours.shortDescription: A classic Cordillera Blanca trek with campsites, glacial lakes, and a crossing of the Punta Unión pass.
tours.description: A mountain program for acclimatized travelers who want to experience a genuine expedition inside Huascarán National Park. The Santa Cruz route links ravines, Andean communities, high-altitude campsites, glacial lakes, and — weather permitting — views of snow-capped peaks such as Taulliraju, Artesonraju, Alpamayo, and Huascarán. It's a demanding, scenic option, ideal for travelers looking for a multi-day trek.
highlights: Classic Santa Cruz Trek route
Punta Unión pass at 4,750 m (15,584 ft)
Mountain campsites
Views of snow-capped peaks and glacial lakes
A demanding experience for acclimatized travelers
includes: Pre-trek briefing in Huaraz
Tourist transport Huaraz – trailhead – Huaraz
Trekking guide
Group camping equipment: dining tent, kitchen tent, and cookware
Shared double tent along the route, subject to availability
Cook and meals during the trek: breakfasts, lunches, and dinners along the route
Muleteers, pack animals, or logistical support as confirmed for the trip
Basic first-aid kit and support throughout the hike
excludes: Hotel accommodation in Huaraz before or after the trek
Entrance fee to Huascarán National Park
Sleeping bag, trekking poles, and personal gear
First breakfast and last dinner in Huaraz

itinerary.title: Huaraz – Llanganuco – Vaquería – Paria
itinerary.description: Early departure from Huaraz through the Callejón de Huaylas, passing through Yungay and the Llanganuco area. After entering Huascarán National Park, the route continues to Vaquería, where the hike begins through Andean valleys to the first campsite in Paria.
details: Approximate altitude: Huaraz 3,050 m (10,007 ft) / Vaquería 3,700 m (12,139 ft) / Paria 3,870 m (12,697 ft).
Approximate hiking time: 3 to 4 hours, at an acclimatization pace.
Main scenery: high-Andean villages, green ravines, and the first views of the Cordillera Blanca.

itinerary.title: Paria – Punta Unión Pass – Taullipampa
itinerary.description: The main day of the trek. A gradual climb leads to the Punta Unión pass, the highest point of the route, with panoramic views of mountains, lakes, and glacial valleys. The trail then descends to the Taullipampa campsite.
details: Approximate maximum altitude: Punta Unión 4,750 m (15,584 ft).
A demanding day due to altitude and elevation gain; good acclimatization is recommended.
Possible views of Taulliraju, Artesonraju, Rinrijirca, and other snow-capped peaks, weather permitting.

itinerary.title: Taullipampa – Mountain Viewpoints – Llamacorral
itinerary.description: A hike through the Santa Cruz valley past lakes, streams, and natural viewpoints. Depending on the group's pace, there may be short side trips or scenic stops to admire snow-capped peaks and lakes before reaching the Llamacorral campsite.
details: A scenic route, less demanding than the Punta Unión day, but still at high altitude.
Possible views of Alpamayo and high-Andean lakes, depending on the route and weather.
Approximate hiking time: 5 to 6 hours.

itinerary.title: Llamacorral – Cashapampa – Return to Huaraz
itinerary.description: The final descent down the valley to Cashapampa. Meet the transport for the drive back to Huaraz. Arrival in the afternoon marks the end of trekking services.
details: Approximate final hiking time: 3 to 4 hours.
Gradual descent toward the village of Cashapampa.
Arrival time in Huaraz depends on the group's pace and road conditions.

tours.title: Matsés National Reserve Expedition 6D/5N
tours.shortDescription: A six-day river expedition to Matsés National Reserve, in the Tapiche, Blanco, and Gálvez river basin: more than two days of river travel each way to reach one of the least-visited territories in the Peruvian Amazon.
tours.description: Matsés National Reserve protects nearly 420,000 hectares of terra firme forest, flooded forest, and varillales in the province of Requena, on the ancestral territory of the indigenous Matsés people, along the border with Brazil. This is not a conventional tourist destination: reaching it requires several days of river travel from Iquitos — first along the Marañón and Ucayali rivers to Requena, then, in smaller and slower boats, along the Tapiche and Blanco rivers to the Curinga ranger checkpoint at the edge of the reserve. This 6-day program is designed as a realistic introduction to the reserve — not a deep journey to the most remote Matsés communities, which require expeditions of 12 days or more — and combines river travel, environmental-interpretation walks with a local guide, and, subject to prior authorization, a possible glimpse of Matsés culture. It's a trip recommended for travelers with a genuine interest in conservation, nature photography, or documentary projects, with realistic expectations about the physical effort and logistics involved.
highlights: One of the least-visited protected areas in the Peruvian Amazon
River travel along the Marañón, Ucayali, Tapiche, and Blanco rivers
Terra firme forest, aguaje palm swamps, and varillales with high wildlife diversity
Ancestral territory of the indigenous Matsés people
SERNANP ranger checkpoint and park guards in Curinga
Expedition format: recommended for experienced travelers, not a conventional tourist circuit
includes: Coordination and processing of SERNANP entry authorization
Overland transport Iquitos-Nauta and river transport Nauta-Requena-Curinga-Requena-Nauta-Iquitos (boats vary by leg)
Local specialist guide, with support from a Matsés guide when operations allow
Accommodation in Requena (basic hostel) and at a rustic camp or lodge in or near the reserve
Full board throughout the expedition
Group camping gear (tents or mosquito nets, depending on the leg)
Entry permit for Matsés National Reserve
excludes: Accommodation in Iquitos before or after the expedition
Travel and medical evacuation insurance (strongly recommended given the distance from medical services)
Tips for guides, boat drivers, and support staff
Personal expedition gear (rubber boots, insect repellent, flashlight, sleeping bag)
Donations or exchanges arranged directly with the Matsés community visited

itinerary.title: Iquitos - Nauta - Requena
itinerary.description: Overland transfer from Iquitos to Nauta, then a fast boat along the Marañón and Ucayali rivers to the city of Requena, the river gateway to the reserve. In the afternoon, a final stock-up on fresh supplies and an equipment check with the guide. Overnight rest in Requena before starting the longest river leg of the trip.
details: Departure from Iquitos to Nauta between 7:00 and 8:00 am
Nauta-Requena river travel, approximately 3 hours by fast boat
Briefing and equipment check in Requena at dusk
itinerary.distance: Overland approx. 1.5 h + river travel approx. 3 h

itinerary.title: River travel on the Tapiche and Blanco rivers
itinerary.description: A full day of river travel aboard a peque-peque motorboat (slower, but suited to narrow rivers), heading up the Tapiche River and then the Blanco River into the interior of Requena province. The landscape gradually shifts from riverside farms to unbroken forest; river birds, monkeys, and occasionally river dolphins are commonly spotted in the wider stretches.
details: Departure from Requena early, around 6:00 am
8 to 10 hours of river travel depending on water levels, with stretch breaks
Overnight at a riverside camp or aboard the outfitted boat

itinerary.title: Entering Matsés National Reserve - Curinga ranger checkpoint
itinerary.description: River travel continues along the Blanco River to the Curinga ranger checkpoint, where SERNANP staff register the group's entry and give a briefing on reserve regulations. Once inside the protected area, take the first orientation walk through terra firme forest, guided by the local team, focused on tracks, birdsong, and notable trees.
details: Estimated arrival in Curinga around midday
Check-in and welcome briefing from SERNANP park rangers
Environmental-interpretation walk of 2 to 3 hours in the afternoon
itinerary.distance: River travel approx. 3-4 h + walking approx. 2-3 h

itinerary.title: Exploring the reserve: forests, varillales, and wildlife
itinerary.description: A day devoted to exploring the area around the checkpoint: walks through varillales (forests on white sand, with low, distinctive vegetation) and flooded forests where taricaya and charapa turtles nest between July and September. Depending on prior coordination with community authorities, a brief encounter with Matsés artisans or reserve collaborators may be included; this contact is not guaranteed and depends on the community's availability and authorization.
details: Early departure, around 6:30 am, to make the most of peak wildlife activity
Combined walk of 4 to 5 hours with observation stops
Possible cultural activity with the Matsés in the afternoon, subject to prior coordination

itinerary.title: Beginning the return: Curinga - Blanco River - Tapiche River
itinerary.description: The long journey back begins, navigating downstream along the Blanco and Tapiche rivers, a day in which the guide continues pointing out wildlife and answers questions about the reserve's biology and conservation status. The descent is faster than the climb upriver, but it's still a full day of river travel.
details: Departure from Curinga early in the morning
Downstream river travel of approximately 6 to 8 hours
Overnight again at a riverside camp or aboard the boat

itinerary.title: Requena - Nauta - Iquitos
itinerary.description: A final river leg to Requena, then a fast boat along the Ucayali and Marañón rivers to Nauta, followed by an overland transfer to Iquitos. Estimated arrival in the afternoon. It's recommended not to schedule departure flights before the evening of the return day, since the river itinerary depends on weather and water levels.
details: Arrival in Requena in the morning
Requena-Nauta river travel, approximately 3 hours
Overland transfer Nauta-Iquitos, with estimated arrival between 3:00 and 5:00 pm
itinerary.distance: River travel approx. 3 h + overland approx. 1.5 h

tours.title: Yaguas National Park Expedition 7D/6N
tours.shortDescription: A seven-day river expedition to Yaguas National Park, in the lower Putumayo River basin: the area with the greatest diversity of freshwater fish in Peru, reachable only after several days of river travel from Iquitos.
tours.description: Yaguas National Park protects nearly 869,000 hectares in the far north of Loreto, between the Putumayo and Amazon rivers, on the border with Colombia. It is renowned for its roughly 337 recorded fish species — about two-thirds of Peru's freshwater fish diversity — along with giant otters, pink and gray river dolphins, black caimans, and a remarkable diversity of birds. Because of its remote location and the absence of permanent tourist infrastructure, access is only possible through organized expeditions: you first navigate down the Amazon River from Iquitos to the Putumayo basin, then head up that river and the Yaguas River to the SERNANP checkpoint at Hipona, passing communities of the indigenous Yagua people such as Primavera and El Álamo. This 7-day program is honest about the fact that much of the time is spent navigating — up to four days round trip — leaving two to three days to explore the heart of the park; it's designed for travelers with a genuine interest in aquatic biodiversity, wildlife watching, nature photography, or conservation projects, not a conventional tourist-paced tour.
highlights: Greatest diversity of freshwater fish in Peru (nearly 337 recorded species)
One of the most pristine, least-disturbed rivers in the Amazon
Chance to spot giant otters, pink river dolphins, and black caimans
Contact with communities of the indigenous Yagua people along the route
SERNANP ranger checkpoint at Hipona, inside the park
Multi-day river expedition format: for experienced travelers only
includes: Coordination and processing of SERNANP entry authorization
Full river transport Iquitos-Putumayo basin-Yaguas National Park-Iquitos
Guide specialized in Amazon wildlife and rivers
Accommodation in a riverside community, campsite, or outfitted boat, depending on the leg
Full board throughout the expedition
Group river-travel and camping equipment
Entry permit for Yaguas National Park
excludes: Accommodation in Iquitos before or after the expedition
Travel and medical evacuation insurance (essential given the distance from emergency services)
Tips for guides, boat drivers, and communities
Personal expedition gear (rubber boots, insect repellent, flashlight, sleeping bag, rain gear)
Donations or exchanges arranged directly with the communities visited

itinerary.title: Iquitos - river travel on the Amazon River
itinerary.description: Board in Iquitos and begin navigating downstream along the Amazon River, passing riverside towns such as Indiana and Pevas. It's a long day of river travel in which the landscape shifts from farmland and clearings to unbroken forest, with good chances of spotting pink and gray river dolphins in the river's widest stretches.
details: Boarding in Iquitos between 6:00 and 7:00 am
Approximately 9 to 10 hours of river travel to the Pevas or San Pablo de Loreto area
Overnight in a riverside town or aboard the outfitted boat

itinerary.title: Toward the Putumayo basin
itinerary.description: River travel continues to the mouth of the Putumayo River, then the first stretch heading upriver, now in the border zone with Colombia. The group passes communities of the indigenous Yagua people, where, depending on prior coordination, a brief courtesy stop may take place before continuing toward the park.
details: Early departure, around 6:00 am
7 to 9 hours of river travel heading up the Putumayo River
Possible stop at a riverside Yagua community in the afternoon

itinerary.title: Up the Yaguas River - entering the park
itinerary.description: Leave the main channel of the Putumayo to head up the Yaguas River, notably clear-watered and lower-flow, to the Hipona ranger checkpoint, where SERNANP registers the group's entry into the national park. This is the point where wildlife watching in a truly pristine setting really begins.
details: 5 to 7 hours of river travel along the Yaguas River
Check-in and briefing with SERNANP park rangers at Hipona
First short orientation walk at dusk

itinerary.title: Exploring the park: oxbow lakes and flooded forest
itinerary.description: A day devoted to exploring oxbow lakes and flooded forests near the checkpoint, by canoe and on foot, in search of giant otters, waterbirds, caimans, and the astonishing fish diversity that makes the park famous. The guide explains the community-based management of the paiche (arapaima) that neighboring communities carry out as a model of sustainable resource use.
details: Departure by canoe to a nearby oxbow lake starting at 6:30 am
Wildlife watching and observational fishing during the morning
Walk through flooded forest in the afternoon
itinerary.distance: Canoe travel and walking, approx. 4-5 h

itinerary.title: Second day of exploration: terra firme forest
itinerary.description: Navigate a further stretch of the Yaguas River toward areas farther from the checkpoint to explore terra firme forest, with a greater chance of finding jaguar tracks, herds of white-lipped peccaries, or troops of monkeys. It's the most remote day of the expedition inside the park, and also a reminder of just how isolated the place is: there's no cell signal or electricity beyond what the team brings itself.
details: River travel to the exploration area, approximately 2 to 3 hours
Wildlife-interpretation walk of 3 to 4 hours
Return to base camp before nightfall
itinerary.distance: River travel approx. 2-3 h + walking approx. 3-4 h

itinerary.title: Beginning the return: Yaguas River and Putumayo River
itinerary.description: The descent begins: navigate back down the Yaguas River to the Putumayo, then downstream toward its mouth, riding the current. The guide reviews the wildlife and plant sightings recorded with the group during the expedition.
details: Departure from the checkpoint early in the morning
Downstream river travel of approximately 8 to 10 hours
Overnight in a riverside community or aboard the boat before the final leg

itinerary.title: Putumayo - Amazon - Iquitos
itinerary.description: The final and longest leg of river travel, descending the Amazon River to Iquitos. Estimated arrival in the late afternoon or evening, so it's recommended not to schedule departure flights the same day; the full river itinerary depends on water levels and weather conditions, and may vary by one or two additional days.
details: Departure before dawn, around 5:00 am, to make the most of the full day
10 to 12 hours of river travel to Iquitos
Estimated arrival between 5:00 and 7:00 pm, with a final transfer to the hotel or airport

itinerary.title: Callejón de Huaylas, Campo Santo de Yungay, Llanganuco, and Caraz
itinerary.description: Reception at the terminal, transfer to your chosen hotel, and departure along the Callejón de Huaylas. Take in Andean villages and views of the Cordillera Blanca and Cordillera Negra ranges, including Huascarán peak. Visit Carhuaz, Mancos, Yungay, the Campo Santo memorial, and Huascarán National Park to see Lake Llanganuco, with time for short walks, photos, and optional activities like boating or horseback riding, depending on local operations. Return via Caraz and the Taricá craft shops.
details: Approximate schedule: reception at 6:00 AM, breakfast at 8:00 AM, departure at 9:00 AM.
Includes scenic stops, a cultural visit, and local tastings, subject to availability.
Estimated arrival in Huaraz: 7:00 PM.

itinerary.title: Chavín de Huántar, Lake Querococha, and the Chavín National Museum
itinerary.description: Departure for the ancient temple of Chavín, passing through Recuay, Ticapampa, and Cátac. Stop at Lake Querococha for photos and to see its natural formation resembling the map of Peru, then cross the Cahuish tunnel into the Conchucos valley. Visit the Chavín Archaeological Monument, its galleries and ceremonial plazas, the Cabezas Clava (tenon heads), the Lanzón de Chavín, and the Chavín National Museum.
details: Approximate schedule: breakfast at 8:00 AM, departure at 9:00 AM.
A cultural journey through high-Andean landscapes and villages of the Conchucos valley.
Estimated arrival in Huaraz: 7:00 PM.

itinerary.title: Pastoruri Glacier, Puya Raimondi, and Rock Art
itinerary.description: Excursion along the Climate Change Route to the Pastoruri sector. Along the way, visit Recuay, Ticapampa, Cátac, the Pachacoto ravine, Lake Patococha, the Pumashim sparkling springs, Puya Raimondi plants, high-altitude springs, and rock art. A short walk leads to views of the Pastoruri glacier, ice caves, and a frozen lake, weather permitting.
details: Approximate schedule: breakfast at 8:00 AM, departure at 9:00 AM.
High altitude; walk slowly, dress warmly, and stay hydrated.
Estimated arrival in Huaraz: 6:00 PM.

itinerary.title: Huaraz City Tour, Willcahuaín, and Monterrey Hot Springs
itinerary.description: A tour of Huaraz and its surroundings: the main square, the Sanctuary of the Lord of Soledad, Jr. José Olaya street, a natural lookout point over Huaraz, the Paria countryside, the Willcahuaín archaeological complex and its site museum, and the Monterrey hot springs. Free afternoon for the craft market, followed by transfer to the terminal at the scheduled time.
details: Approximate schedule: breakfast at 8:00 AM, departure at 10:00 AM or 2:00 PM depending on operations.
Approximate duration: 4 hours.
Optional, subject to coordination: Honcopampa, Yuracyacu waterfall, and Chancos hot springs.

itinerary.title: Laguna 69 Trek from Cebollapampa
itinerary.description: Early-morning departure north from Huaraz through the Callejón de Huaylas, passing through Yungay and entering Huascarán National Park. The route crosses the Llanganuco ravine and its lakes to Cebollapampa, the starting point of the hike. The trek climbs through ravines, waterfalls, and high-Andean flora, with views of snow-capped peaks such as Huascarán, Huandoy, Yanapaccha, Pisco, and Chacraraju, all the way to Laguna 69, at roughly 4,600 m (15,090 ft) above sea level. Return along the same trail back to Huaraz.
details: Approximate schedule: departure at 5:00 AM, return around 7:00 PM.
Moderate to challenging hike due to altitude: 6 to 7 hours round trip, depending on pace.
A box lunch, water, warm clothing, rain gear, trekking poles, and sunscreen are recommended.
itinerary.meals: Breakfast and box lunch not included unless confirmed
itinerary.distance: Approx. 8 km (5 mi) ascent / 6 to 7 hours round trip

itinerary.title: Callejón de Huaylas, Campo Santo de Yungay, Llanganuco, and Caraz
itinerary.description: Reception at the terminal, transfer to your chosen hotel, and departure along the Callejón de Huaylas. Take in Andean villages and views of the Cordillera Blanca and Cordillera Negra ranges, including Huascarán peak. Visit Carhuaz, Mancos, Yungay, the Campo Santo memorial, and Huascarán National Park to see Lake Llanganuco, with time for short walks, photos, and optional activities like boating or horseback riding, depending on local operations. Return via Caraz and the Taricá craft shops.
details: Approximate schedule: reception at 6:00 AM, breakfast at 8:00 AM, departure at 9:00 AM.
Includes scenic stops, a cultural visit, and local tastings, subject to availability.

itinerary.title: Chavín de Huántar, Lake Querococha, and the Chavín National Museum
itinerary.description: Departure for the ancient temple of Chavín, passing through Recuay, Ticapampa, and Cátac. Stop at Lake Querococha for photos and to see its natural formation resembling the map of Peru, then cross the Cahuish tunnel into the Conchucos valley. Visit the Chavín Archaeological Monument, its galleries and ceremonial plazas, the Cabezas Clava (tenon heads), the Lanzón de Chavín, and the Chavín National Museum.
details: Approximate schedule: breakfast at 8:00 AM, departure at 9:00 AM.
A cultural journey through high-Andean landscapes and villages of the Conchucos valley.
Estimated arrival in Huaraz: 7:00 PM.

itinerary.title: Pastoruri Glacier, Puya Raimondi, and Rock Art
itinerary.description: Excursion along the Climate Change Route to the Pastoruri sector. Along the way, visit Recuay, Ticapampa, Cátac, the Pachacoto ravine, Lake Patococha, the Pumashim sparkling springs, Puya Raimondi plants, high-altitude springs, and rock art. A short walk leads to views of the Pastoruri glacier, ice caves, and a frozen lake, weather permitting.
details: Approximate schedule: breakfast at 8:00 AM, departure at 9:00 AM.
High altitude; walk slowly, dress warmly, and stay hydrated.
Estimated arrival in Huaraz: 6:00 PM.

tours.title: Pachacámac Essentials: Sanctuary, Green Valley & Town
tours.shortDescription: A full-day trip from Lima featuring the Pachacámac Archaeological Sanctuary, the historic town center, a valley viewpoint and a country-style lunch.
tours.description: A cultural and scenic experience designed to discover Pachacámac beyond a quick visit to the sanctuary. The route connects the central coast’s major pre-Hispanic ceremonial center with the traditional town of Pachacámac, its historic church, the countryside of the Lurín Valley and one of its viewpoints. It is ideal for travelers looking for archaeology, local cuisine and a relaxed day trip from Lima.

tours.title: Lomas de Lúcumo + Rural Pachacámac Full Day
tours.shortDescription: Guided trekking at Lomas de Lúcumo, a country-style lunch and a scenic route through the Pachacámac Valley.
tours.description: A nature-focused full day near Lima built around the Lomas de Lúcumo Ecotourism Circuit in Quebrada Verde. It includes a hike with a local guide, time for lunch in Pachacámac and a relaxed route through the town and valley. Access and the lush green appearance of the lomas are seasonal, so operations are always reconfirmed with the local association before accepting a booking.
